32194.s: The bill amends the Criminal Code and Code of Criminal Procedure to strengthen the confiscation of unlawfully obtained advantage: it adds a rebuttable presumption that expenditure and assets acquired in the six years before an offence derive from crime, expands conservatory seizure of third-party assets, and creates a post-conviction investigation into a convicted person's assets with coercive powers (observation, communications interception, entry into non-residential premises), authorised by the investigating judge. It also sets a six-week deadline for confiscation judgments and allows general administrative orders on written preparation of confiscation proceedings.
32194.j: The memorandum justifies the new powers by the gap between imposed confiscation amounts and what is actually recovered, and states that the investigating judge's mandate and proportionality review, plus judicial oversight and notification duties, guard against arbitrary interference with privacy under Article 8 ECHR.
q: I therefore consider it necessary to strengthen the criminal-procedure recovery powers for cases where there is reason to suppose the convicted person is able but unwilling to pay his payment obligation.

Ik acht een versterking van de strafvorderlijke verhaalsbevoegdheden in dit verband derhalve noodzakelijk voor die gevallen waarin er aanleiding bestaat om te veronderstellen dat de veroordeelde wel in staat maar onwillig is om aan zijn betalingsverplichting te voldoen.
d: rules on written preparation of confiscation proceedings
p: Investigating officers may, on the prosecutor's order, demand asset information from third parties, conduct systematic observation, intercept non-public communications and enter non-residential premises without the owner's consent to trace a convicted person's assets.
A post-conviction asset investigation may be opened on the prosecutor's request and a judicial mandate from the investigating judge, which is time-limited to six months and extendable to two years.
Artikel I, onderdeel B (art. 36e lid 3 Sr)

A rebuttable presumption shifts the burden to convicted persons to show a legal origin for expenditure and assets acquired in the six years before the offence, though the judge may shorten this period.
Artikel II, onderdeel A (art. 94a lid 3 Sv)

Conservatory seizure is extended to objects belonging to third parties where there are sufficient indications of an intent to frustrate recovery and the third party knew or could reasonably suspect this.
Artikel II, onderdeel B (art. 126a lid 5 Sv)
Persons served with a financial-investigation demand must keep the information confidential in the interest of the investigation.

parties: Asks whether the 'aanzienlijk belang' criterion for investigating the convict's assets is clear enough and whether the six-year period is justified, while supporting the bill's aim.
At the same time they ask whether this criterion is sufficiently clear in practice.
Tegelijkertijd vragen zij of dit criterium in de praktijk duidelijk genoeg is.
Asks how a statutory presumption differs from a reversal of the burden of proof and how a reasonable allocation of the burden can be guaranteed.
Supports confiscation but insists that no more than unlawfully obtained gain is seized and that the convict has a fair chance to prove legal origin of assets.
They emphasise, however, that the aim of the bill must also be that no more is confiscated than was obtained through criminal offences.
Wel benadrukken zij dat het doel van het wetsvoorstel ook moet zijn dat niet meer wordt ontnomen dan door strafbare feiten is verkregen.
Asks when applying the presumption would produce manifestly unjust results and whether the threshold of a fifth-category fine is appropriate; wants judges to motivate deviations from the claim.
These members ask when application of that would lead to manifestly unjust results.
Deze leden vragen wanneer toepassing daarvan tot apert onrechtvaardige resultaten zou leiden.
Supports broader confiscation and the reversal of the burden on the convict's origin of assets, and doubts whether expertise and culture will deliver the intended results.
By requiring in such cases that a convicted person give insight into the origin of his assets, in these members' view the effectiveness of this bill increases considerably.

Door in die gevallen van een veroordeelde te verlangen dat hij inzicht geeft in de herkomst van zijn vermogen, neemt naar het oordeel van deze leden de effectiviteit van dit wetsvoorstel aanzienlijk toe.

Accepts a statutory presumption within reasonable limits but questions the requirement that other offences contributed to the gain and whether confiscating lawfully obtained assets fits the aim of the measure.
Does confiscation of lawfully obtained assets fit the aim of confiscating only unlawfully obtained gain?
Ontneming van legaal verkregen vermogen wel bij de doelstelling om (slechts) wederrechtelijk verkregen voordeel te ontnemen?

v.summary: The Raad van State advised negatively on the draft bill expanding confiscation of unlawfully obtained advantage (ontneming), raising concerns about the travel ban, reversed burden of proof, anderbeslag, and the investigation of convicted persons' assets. The government's nader rapport accepts most points, drops the travel ban, narrows the reversed burden and anderbeslag, and adds judicial safeguards.
concerns: The travel ban as a supplementary penalty was found disproportionate and insufficiently justified, and the government dropped it from the bill.

The reversed burden of proof with a six-year lookback and no required criminal link was seen as too broad; the government clarified the principle and allowed the judge to shorten the period ex officio.
Expanded anderbeslag risked infringing property rights of good-faith third parties; the government added a knowledge requirement but kept the 'aanwijzingen' criterion.

The necessity of the changes was not convincingly demonstrated given evaluations pointing to under-application rather than legislative gaps; the government added justification but did not fully resolve this.
Investigative powers into a convicted person's assets were left too open-ended; the government now enumerates powers and conditions in the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Various drafting and terminology points, such as 'verhaalsfrustratie' and cross-references, were adopted in the reply.
Earlier consultation with advisory bodies was not repeated for the substantially changed bill, and the Raad asked for justification of this.

32222-III.s: The bill amends the 2009 budget statutes of the Ministry of General Affairs, the Royal Cabinet and the Oversight Committee for the intelligence and security services, mainly by reallocating funds and adding wage and price adjustments. It sets the amended budget figures in thousands of euros and enters into force on 1 December 2009, with retroactive effect where the Staatsblad appears later.
q: The present bill aims to make changes to the 2009 budget statutes of the Ministry of General Affairs, the Royal Cabinet and the Oversight Committee for the intelligence and security services (III).

Het onderhavige wetsvoorstel strekt ertoe om voor het jaar 2009 wijzigingen aan te brengen in de begrotingsstaten van het Ministerie van Algemene Zaken, het Kabinet der Koningin en de Commissie van toezicht betreffende de inlichtingen- en veiligheidsdiensten (III).

32257.s: The bill implements EU framework decision 2008/675/JBZ by extending Dutch criminal-law recidive provisions in the Criminal Code, Code of Criminal Procedure and several special statutes to final convictions handed down by criminal courts in other EU member states for similar offences. It leaves judges' discretion unchanged and does not create new executive delegations.
32257.j: The memorandum justifies the changes as required to implement the framework decision and to let prosecutors and judges take a fuller criminal record into account, while stressing that judges keep their discretion.
q: The judge therefore keeps the same discretion regarding foreign convictions as regarding Dutch convictions.
De rechter behoudt dus de beoordelingsvrijheid die hij heeft ten aanzien van Nederlandse veroordelingen, ook ten aanzien van buitenlandse veroordelingen.

parties: Asks whether leaving retrieval of foreign criminal records optional could create legal inequality and conflict with the EVRM, and about prison capacity effects.
The CDA members ask whether this could lead to legal inequality and whether it could conflict with the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR).

De leden van de CDA-fractie vragen of dit kan leiden tot rechtsongelijkheid en of dit strijd met het Europees Verdrag tot Bescherming van de Rechten voor de Mens en Fundamentele Vrijheden (EVRM) zou kunnen opleveren.
Asks for clarification on whether legal persons fall under the framework decision and whether amending article 63 Sr could disadvantage or benefit defendants.
The PvdA members, with the Dutch Bar Association (NOvA), believe the framework decision does not show that it also applies to legal persons.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie zijn met de Nederlandse Orde van Advocaten (NOvA) van mening dat uit het kaderbesluit niet blijkt dat deze ook van toepassing is op rechtspersonen.

Worries about blind trust in foreign convictions, the reliability of exchanged criminal record data, rights to challenge wrong registrations, and whether non-EU convictions should be treated differently.
These members believe this must not mean the criminal judge has to trust convictions in other member states blindly without being allowed to place critical reservations.
Deze leden zijn van mening dat dit niet mag betekenen dat de strafrechter blind moet vertrouwen op veroordelingen in andere lidstaten zonder daar kritische kanttekeningen bij te mogen plaatsen.

v.summary: The Council of State broadly supports the bill implementing framework decision 2008/675/JBZ on taking account of foreign convictions in new criminal proceedings, but asks whether the Dutch concurrence rule (article 63 Sr) must be adapted in light of recitals 8 and 9, and asks the explanatory memorandum to clarify how the last paragraph of article 3(5) will be implemented. The minister replies that article 63 Sr need not be amended because it only applies to concurrent offences and foreign sentences are often not comparable, that Dutch judges remain free to take prior foreign convictions into account, and that the explanatory memorandum has been supplemented accordingly.
concerns: The Council is not yet convinced that article 63 Sr need not be amended in view of recitals 8 and 9, which seek to avoid less favourable treatment of offenders than with domestic convictions; the minister disagrees but accepts the need for explanation.
The explanatory memorandum should clarify how the last paragraph of article 3(5) of the framework decision is given effect; the memorandum was supplemented accordingly.

32356.s: The bill harmonises the reporting deadline for absence at 4 weeks across education laws and moves supervision of schools' compliance with the Compulsory Education Act 1969 from municipalities to the Inspectorate of Education, replacing the criminal sanction with an administrative fine of up to 1000 euro per violation. It also lets municipal bodies in joint arrangements receive reports and requires schools to include an absence policy in their prospectus or education agreement.
32356.j: The memorandum justifies moving supervision to the Inspectorate by its greater independence, distance from local politics, and better equipment for the task, and justifies the administrative fine as better suited to a supervisory relationship than a criminal sanction.
q: Supervision of schools' compliance with the Compulsory Education Act 1969 is insufficiently effective.
Het toezicht op de naleving van de Lpw 1969 door scholen is onvoldoende effectief.
d: designated body under joint arrangement receives absence notifications
p: Supervision of schools' compliance with the Leerplichtwet moves from municipalities to the national Inspectorate of Education, shifting oversight authority to a national executive body.
The Minister may impose administrative fines of up to 1000 euro per violation on school heads, replacing a criminal sanction with an administrative sanction.

parties: Asks why the individual school head rather than the governing body is sanctioned, echoing the Council of State, and whether the Inspectorate has capacity and suitability for new supervisory tasks.
However, these members ask, as the Council of State has also noted, whether the head of the school should be burdened with this.
Wel vragen deze leden, zoals ook de Raad van State al heeft opgemerkt, of het hoofd van de school hiermee belast moet worden.
Welcomes shifting supervision to the independent Inspectorate and calls for stricter oversight of schools failing reporting deadlines, while worrying that municipalities lose grip on enforcement.
The members therefore consider it good that supervision will be carried out by the Inspectorate of Education.
De leden vinden het daarom goed dat het toezicht gaat worden uitgevoerd door de onderwijsinspectie.

Asks how the Inspectorate, which visits schools only about once every four years and works at a distance, will detect unreported absence and whether its risk-based approach will cover fraud in reporting.
Is it wise to transfer supervision of absence reporting to a body that is much further away from the school?
Is het verstandig om het toezicht op het melden van verzuim over te dragen aan een instantie die veel verder weg van de school staat?
Asks how supervision based on trust will work and whether the Inspectorate, dependent on municipal signals, can enforce effectively.
Is therefore the quality of enforcement and supervision not still dependent on municipal effort?
Is daarmee ook niet de kwaliteit van handhaving en toezicht nog steeds afhankelijk van gemeentelijke inzet?

Questions whether the Inspectorate's risk analysis will improve enforcement of the compulsory education act, given that truancy enforcement is only a small part of its risk analysis, and asks why criminal penalties for responsible persons were not converted to administrative fines.
They note that enforcement of the Compulsory Education Act will be only a limited part of the risk analysis, while for truancy officers it is one of the main tasks.
Zij merken op dat de handhaving van de Leerplichtwet in de risicoanalyse slechts een beperkt onderdeel zal zijn, terwijl het voor leerplichtambtenaren een van de hoofdtaken is.

v.summary: The Council of State advised that the bill shifting supervision of schools' compliance with the Compulsory Education Act from municipalities to the Inspectorate, and replacing criminal sanctions for school heads with administrative fines, be reconsidered in part. The government's reply rejects the objections on supervision, adds justification, and largely accepts the advice on sanction motivation and the placement of the head of school as addressee.
concerns: The Council doubts that shifting supervision of schools from municipalities to the Inspectorate is necessary and effective, and asks for reconsideration of the proposal.
The Council finds that the choice of administrative rather than criminal sanctions lacks adequate motivation and that the sanction should be grounded in the nature of the offence.
The Council notes that an administrative sanction aimed at the individual school head sits uneasily with the education law system, where sanctions are aimed at the competent authority.
The Council gives a redactional comment proposing that the notice period of five weeks be changed to four weeks in several provisions.

32360-X.s: This bill amends the 2009 budget statements of the Ministry of Defence and of the three baten-lastendiensten (Defensie Telematica Organisatie, Dienst Vastgoed Defensie and Paresto), adopting the final budget adjustment (slotwet) for that year. It sets amounts in thousands of euros and provides for retroactive entry into force to 31 December of the budget year, without delegating rule-making power.
q: The departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Defence (X) for the year 2009 is amended, as shown in the statement annexed to this act.
De departementale begrotingsstaat van het Ministerie van Defensie (X) voor het jaar 2009 wordt gewijzigd, zoals blijkt uit de desbetreffende bij deze wet behorende staat.

32374.s: The bill amends the Electricity Act 1998 and the Gas Act to adjust the smart meter rollout, making remote-readable meters optional for consumers rather than mandatory and shifting installation and fee rules to ministerial and general administrative orders. It also allows ministerial rules on limiting electricity supply and on transferring tariff payments between suppliers and grid operators.
32374.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations as needed to set detailed technical and tariff rules that align with sector processes and tax rules, and to make rollout percentages and supply limitation conditions workable.
q: Further rules on any large-scale rollout will be laid down by general administrative order.
Nadere regels over de eventuele grootschalige uitrol zullen bij algemene maatregel van bestuur worden vastgelegd.
d: percentage of customers to receive remote-readable meters during rollout
compensation amounts for meter takeover, varying by situation
rules on limiting electricity supply, including when and under what conditions
size and timing of payments by suppliers to grid operators
size and timing of payments by suppliers to grid operators (gas)
p: I, onderdeel J, artikel 26ac (lid 2) and II, onderdeel E, artikel 13c (lid 2)
Consumers may request that meters not be read remotely, restricting the grid operator's reading practice on the consumer's request.
I, onderdeel J, artikel 26ab and II, onderdeel E, artikel 13b
Grid operators may collect metering data on consumers for purposes defined by a ministerial rule, with the conditions set by delegation.</description_en>

parties: Asks whether the amendment truly drops the smart meter obligation and resolves privacy concerns, and whether it meets the intentions expressed in earlier amendments.

These members stress the need to remove the duty to cooperate with the installation of smart meters, as well as the need to write an explicit guarantee of the protection of personal data of small consumers into the law.

Deze leden onderstrepen de noodzaak om de medewerkingsplicht aan de plaatsing van slimme meters te schrappen, evenals de noodzaak tot het in de wet opnemen van een geëxpliciteerde waarborging van de bescherming van persoonsgegevens van kleinverbruikers.
Worries consumers do not know their right to refuse a smart meter and wants a duty on network operators to inform them, and wants the disconnection rule strengthened into firm statutory limits.
These members therefore want the so-called 'may' provision to set further rules on disconnection policy to be turned into a provision that guarantees additional rules will be set.

Deze leden willen dan ook dat de zogenaamde «kan-bepaling» om nadere regels te stellen met betrekking tot het afsluitbeleid wordt omgezet in een bepaling die zeker stelt dat aanvullende regels worden gesteld.

Asks about consequences of a court ruling that the unbundling provisions conflict with EU law, and asks for protection of small consumers against supplier abuse, independent cost-benefit research and a binding model contract.

The SP members ask about the consequences for the bill of the Hague Court of Appeal's ruling of 22 June 2010 on the Unbundling Act, which holds that article 10b of the Electricity Act 1998 and article 2c of the Gas Act conflict with provisions of the EC Treaty.

De leden van de SP-fractie vragen naar de consequenties op het wetsvoorstel van de uitspraak van het Gerechtshof Den Haag van 22 juni 2010 over de Splitsingswet, waarin het Hof stelt dat artikel 10b Elektriciteitswet 1998 en artikel 2c Gaswet in strijd zijn met bepalingen uit het EG-Verdrag.
Argues that privacy objections are a legitimate ground for refusing a smart meter and asks why the mandatory character was not dropped earlier and how the support level is measured.
These members are of the view that personal privacy objections can constitute a legitimate ground for refusing activation of a smart meter.
Deze leden zijn van mening dat persoonlijke bezwaren op vlak van privacy een legitieme grond kunnen vormen om het activeren van een slimme meter te weigeren.
Asks whether privacy safeguards are sufficiently respected when remote readability is switched off and whether consumers always have insight into data flows to energy companies.
The ChristenUnie members attach importance to the essential condition of privacy protection.
De leden van de fractie van de ChristenUnie hechten aan de belangrijke voorwaarde van privacybescherming.

v.summary: The Raad van State advises on a novelle to the bill on smart meters, questioning whether the voluntary rollout and optional remote-reading approach is compatible with Directive 2006/32/EG and the third electricity directive's 80% target, and advising reconsideration and clarification. The minister's reply largely rejects the EU-compatibility objection, keeps the voluntary approach, and explains that the privacy concern is addressed by consent requirements and the ability to switch off remote reading.
concerns: The Raad doubts that the voluntary rollout of smart meters fits Directive 2006/32/EG and the 80% target of the third electricity directive, and suggests a mandatory rollout is closer to their aim.
The Raad notes that a voluntary approach may create uncertainty and costly re-replacement of meters, and asks the government to reconsider the choice to drop mandatory rollout.

The Raad finds the privacy objection largely resolved by the consent requirement and the option to disable remote reading, but asks that standard energy-contract clauses not hollow out the consent requirement.
The Raad asks that the explanatory memorandum explain these choices more fully and that the bill be adjusted where necessary.

32383.s: The bill extends Dutch social security, labour and related legal provisions (child benefit, survivors', old-age, health, unemployment, sickness, minimum wage, collective agreements, court jurisdiction and childcare) to workers on the Dutch continental shelf, defined as the EEZ adjacent to the Dutch territorial sea. It also repeals the Wet arbeid mijnbouw Noordzee and assigns the Alkmaar district court jurisdiction over related labour disputes.
32383.j: The memorandum justifies the extension by noting the workers' need for social security coverage and the European Commission's demands, and it addresses enforcement concerns raised by the SVB, CVZ and employers without creating new executive discretion.
q: Without government control over premium payments on the NCP, foreign employers in particular could devise structures to avoid paying premiums.
Bij gebrek aan controle door de overheid op de afdracht van premies op het NCP zouden vooral buitenlandse werkgevers constructies kunnen optuigen om onder de premieafdracht uit te kunnen komen.
d: date of entry into force by royal decree

parties: Asks how the law will be enforced and by whom, and whether self-employed persons will try to avoid premiums.
In what way will this law be enforced and by whom?
Op welke wijze zal deze wet worden gehandhaafd en door wie?
Asks how enforcement will be organised and what problems are expected.
The PvdA members ask how enforcement of this law will be organised and what problems are expected.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie vragen hoe de handhaving van deze wet wordt vormgegeven en welke problemen daarbij te verwachten zijn.
Supports the goal of better protection but argues for keeping the WAMN principle that Dutch social law applies only where strong Dutch legal ties exist, and questions rejecting a UK-style opt-in.
In the view of the CDA members, this starting point should also serve as a guideline for the present legislation.
Naar het oordeel van de leden van de CDA-fractie moet dit uitgangspunt ook bij de onderhavige wetgeving als leidraad dienen.

32392.s: The bill implements the EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC by amending the Environmental Management Act (Wet milieubeheer), the environmental taxes act and the Economic Offences Act, updating waste definitions, the waste hierarchy, the waste management plan period (six years) and rules on separate collection and mixing bans. It also adds ministerial and general administrative order powers to set rules for reuse, recycling and waste handling, with transitional and commencement provisions.
32392.j: The memorandum justifies delegations mainly as needed to implement the EU directive, with lower-level regulations (productbesluiten, LAP) and EU comitology carrying technical detail.
q: Under Article 29(4) of the directive, the Commission may set indicators for waste prevention measures via a committee procedure.
Krachtens artikel 29, vierde lid, van de richtlijn kunnen door de Commissie via een Comitéprocedure indicatoren voor afvalpreventiemaatregelen worden vastgesteld.
d: exemptions from waste chapter for listed substances
rules for categories of substances, products or waste to stimulate reuse, prevention and recycling
producer responsibility rules for products and residual waste
municipal council may decide on separate collection of waste
obligation of separate collection of household waste where feasible
obligation of separate collection of business or hazardous waste where feasible
cases in which unlawfully mixed hazardous waste must be separated
indicators for monitoring waste prevention measures
amendments to annexes and EU measures applying automatically to waste definitions
ministerial regulation listing substances that count as waste
deviation from waste hierarchy for specific waste streams based on lifecycle assessment
p: Allows the minister to depart from the waste hierarchy for specific waste streams where a lifecycle assessment justifies it.
Lets an executive regulation exclude listed substances and objects from the waste chapter without parliamentary involvement.

parties: Asks whether the law should specify the final recycling goal rather than mandate pre-sorting, and questions double charging under producer responsibility and the five-year retention period.
The members would like the law to specify the ultimate goal and not impose an obligation to separate in advance.
De leden zouden graag zien dat de wet het uiteindelijke doel specificeert en geen verplichting om vooraf te scheiden oplegt.
Asks the government to explain deviations from the directive, the reasons for the wording changes, and the consequences for Dutch waste policy targets.
The CDA members ask the government to explain which minor technical changes deviate from the European directive, why they were chosen, and how this affects the level playing field within the EU.

De leden van de CDA-fractie vragen de regering om uiteen te zetten welke ondergeschikte technische wijzigingen afwijken van de Europese richtlijn, waarom daarvoor gekozen is en hoe dit het gelijke speelveld binnen de Europese Unie beïnvloedt.
Critical of open EU waste trade and the R1 status of incineration; asks how enforcement visibility is preserved and how the government will prevent economic interests from undermining recycling.
How will the government prevent the economic interests of incinerator operators from standing in the way of the transition to a recycling society?
Hoe gaat de regering voorkomen dat de economische belangen van exploitanten van verbrandingsovens de transitie naar een recyclingmaatschappij in de weg staan?

Welcomes the directive but asks about the Council of State advice, the influence of Council, Parliament and the Chamber over the regulatory committee, and the reasons for the five-year retention period and the producer responsibility wording.
Given the fairly broad definition of the powers of the proposed Regulatory Committee, these members ask how the Council, the European Parliament and the Chamber can influence the committee's work.

Gezien de vrij brede definitie van de bevoegdheden van het voorgestelde Regelgevend Comité, vragen deze leden zich af of de regering kan uiteenzetten op welke wijze de Raad, het Europese Parlement en de Kamer invloed hebben op de werkzaamheden van het comité?
Asks why municipal duty covers collection but not processing of household waste, citing legal uncertainty for municipalities, and questions the vague 'partly' wording on producer responsibility.

To prevent municipalities from facing legal proceedings in which the right to process waste is contested, these members suggest amending article 10.21 of the Environmental Management Act so that waste processing also falls under the municipal duty of care.

Om te voorkomen dat gemeenten worden geconfronteerd met juridische procedures waarin het recht tot het verwerken van het afval wordt betwist geven genoemde leden in overweging artikel 10.21 van de Wet milieubeheer zo aan te passen dat ook de afvalverwerking onder de zorgplicht van gemeenten wordt gebracht

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on the draft Implementation Act for the EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC, raising objections on the waste definition, separate collection duties, national registration obligations beyond the directive, and transitional provisions. The government's nader rapport accepted most points, amended the bill and explanatory memorandum, and largely followed the advice.
concerns: Combinations of waste and solvents must remain within the waste definition, so the bill was amended to refer to 'stoffen, preparaten of voorwerpen'.
Mandatory separate collection of paper, metal, plastic and glass by 2015 must be subject to the technical, environmental and economic feasibility criteria, and the Commission should be consulted.
National registration and five-year retention obligations for business and hazardous waste go beyond the directive, so the explanatory memorandum must justify them and address business burdens.
Transitional provisions for the waste management plan and environmental permits needed justification in the explanatory memorandum and were supplemented.
Numerous redactional comments on cross-references, terminology and transposition table were largely followed, with a few not adopted.

32419.s: The bill amends the Aanpassingswet openbare lichamen Bonaire, Sint Eustatius en Saba to adapt a wide set of Dutch education, student finance, higher education, compulsory schooling, and media laws for the Caribbean public bodies, including new Leerplichtwet BES and Mediawet BES provisions. It largely transposes existing Antillean rules into Dutch statutory form with Dutch terminology, leaving most detail to general administrative orders and ministerial regulations.
32419.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations mainly by the need for workable local implementation and by the fact that the Caribbean media sector lacks expertise, so supervision is placed with the Dutch Commissariaat voor de Media rather than local bodies.
q: For the structure of the proposed Wet educatie en beroepsonderwijs BES, the Wet educatie en beroepsonderwijs was used as a model.
Voor de opbouw van het voorstel van Wet educatie en beroepsonderwijs BES is gekeken naar de Wet educatie en beroepsonderwijs.
d: priority rules for overlapping repayment obligations
additional entry requirements for specific programmes
further rules and forms for leerplicht implementation
Leerplichtwet BES art. 3 (advice on school criteria)
bestuurscollege follows inspectorate advice on school status
advertising restrictions for alcohol and tobacco and programme advertising
access to airtime and facilities in emergencies
Prime Minister may set content rules and oversight in general emergency
airtime allocation procedures and total hours for government and party broadcasts
p: In a general state of emergency the Prime Minister may, after consulting the minister, set rules on radio and television content and its supervision and depart from the normal licensing and content articles.
Compulsory schooling enforcement officers may enter schools and other non-residential premises and require cooperation from anyone, with limited statutory safeguards.
Police may take a young person found on a publicly accessible place during school hours back to school.

parties: Asks why Dutch education laws were adopted instead of the Antillean ordinances, how adaptation to island scale is ensured, and how spending under the improvement plan is controlled.
How is it checked that the money is spent properly?
Hoe wordt gecontroleerd dat het geld goed wordt besteed?
Asks whether the bill follows the Raad van State's advice to adapt or drop burdensome provisions, and questions whether the Dutch laws are pitched at too high an abstraction level for the islands.
Has the government sufficiently adopted the Council's advice to adapt or delete Dutch provisions that may be too burdensome for the public bodies?
Heeft de regering het advies van de Raad om Nederlandse bepalingen die te belastend kunnen zijn voor de openbare lichamen aan te passen of te schrappen, voldoende overgenomen?

Supports the Dutch-model approach but asks how enforcement of compulsory schooling will work, whether inspection can act firmly, and requests evaluation of the new law's effects and administrative burden.
The CDA asks whether an evaluation moment is foreseen to assess the feasibility and effects of the new legislation and the administrative burden it brings.

De leden van de CDA-fractie vragen of er een evaluatiemoment is voorzien om de uitvoerbaarheid en de effecten van de nieuwe wetgeving te beoordelen, alsook de administratieve lastendruk die deze met zich meebrengt.

Retains doubts about adopting Dutch education laws as model, questions insufficient attention to island-specific circumstances, and asks about enforcement of compulsory schooling and discretion in school funding and closure norms.
These members note that they continue to have reservations about the government's starting point of taking Dutch education laws as the model for the BES education laws.
Deze leden merken op dat zij bedenkingen blijven houden bij het uitgangspunt van de regering om Nederlandse onderwijswetten te nemen als model voor de BES onderwijswetten.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on the Tweede Aanpassingswet openbare lichamen Bonaire, Sint Eustatius en Saba, raising major objections to the education bills (too model-based on Dutch laws, administratively heavy), the Wet politiegegevens changes, the Centrale Raad van Beroep jurisdiction, and the temporary mismanagement power, among others. The government's nader rapport largely accepted the education and police-data remarks, rejected the jurisdiction change, and explained its reasoning on the other points.
concerns: The Raad found the education bills too modelled on Dutch laws, with many administrative duties ill-suited to small islands; the government simplified and phased obligations but kept the model.

The Raad advised against giving the Centrale Raad van Beroep jurisdiction in the public bodies, as it hollows out the Caribbean judicial structure; the government kept its position with a samenwerking solution.

The Raad objected to the temporary ministerial power to direct school boards for mismanagement and to the reference to the 'kennelijke geest' of statutes; the government made the power structural and removed the interpretive reference.
The Raad questioned whether police-data exchange with Curaçao and Sint Maarten can precede adequate data-protection rules and whether a Landsregeling may depart from a form-free arrangement.
The Raad flagged duplicate statute titles, structure, numbering and readability issues, most of which were corrected.

32428.s: The bill amends the Adaptation Act for the public bodies Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, adapting Netherlands Antillean rules (pensions, social security, labour, financial supervision, nature, traffic, aviation, health and more) so they fit the new Dutch public-body status of the islands. It largely reassigns former Antillean powers to Dutch ministers, the Rijksvertegenwoordiger, the Dutch central bank or the public bodies, and adds numerous subdelegations and rule-making authorities.
32428.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations as needed for flexibility and adaptation during the transition, aligning the islands' rules with Dutch law and allowing later adjustment by ministerial regulation.
q: This gives flexibility and the possibility of interim adjustment during the transitional phase.
Dit geeft flexibiliteit en de mogelijkheid tot tussentijdse bijsturing tijdens de overgangsfase.
d: pension agreement terms set by Minister with unions
rules on duurtetoeslag and kindertoelagen for pensioners
management and security rules for population registry
amount of price-level allowance for pensioners per island
grounds for refusing work permits, exceptions per island
Artikel 42a Wet weduwen- en wezenverzekering BES
implementing rules for breath, saliva and blood tests
establishment of nature parks incl. in exclusive economic zone
how bodies cooperate with ministerial compliance investigation
elements of cost-covering premium, actuarial and technical notes
rules on outsourcing by pension funds
transitional rules for accrued pension rights
p: Crown, after hearing the Council of State, may depart from standard pension rules for the Rijksvertegenwoordiger in special cases.
Artikel 11.25 Wet weduwen- en wezenverzekering BES (art. 26 and 27 lifting of rules)
Removes certain statutory rules and shifts pension and premium matters into ministerial rule-making.
Artikel 12.22 Wet rijbevoegdheid BES (art. 6 onderdeel D)
Gives police officers power to order blood, urine or breath tests and impose short driving bans on suspects, with implementing rules delegated.
Authority may impose administrative fines up to USD 25,000 per violation, after written notice of intent.
Artikel 6.5 Wet melding ongebruikelijke transacties BES
Allows the reporting office to share information on reporting conduct with supervisors and designated bodies.
Minister may investigate municipal and agency compliance with population register rules, with the privacy commission given supervisory role.

parties: Asks why several provisions (e.g., designation of payment bodies, traffic-safety and alcohol limits) are left to ministerial regulation rather than the statute, and how decentralised traffic rules fit with national law.
It is regulated that the possible designation of other bodies that may pay old-age or survivors' pensions is done by ministerial regulation, the VVD members note.

Er wordt geregeld dat de mogelijke aanwijzing van andere organen die het ouderdomspensioen of het weduwen- of wezenpensioen betaalbaar kunnen stellen, geschiedt bij ministeriële regeling, aldus de leden van de VVD-fractie.
Asks questions only on nature management, national park status, budgets and the legal basis for nature protection on the islands.
In connection with this, these members ask whether nature areas on one of the BES islands can claim the status of a (Dutch) National Park?
Naar aanleiding hiervan vragen deze leden of natuurgebieden op een van de BES-eilanden aanspraak kunnen maken op het (Nederlands) Nationaal Park?

Broadly supports the bill but asks whether DNB's recommendations will be followed after the transition, why the Dutch principles for good pension fund governance and an accountability body are not required, and how supervision of labour-migration rules is organised.

The CDA members have noted that the government has not adopted a number of parts of the advice of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) on (supervision of the implementation of) the Company Pension Funds BES Act.

De leden van de CDA-fractie hebben geconstateerd dat de regering een aantal onderdelen van het advies van De Nederlandse Bank (DNB) inzake (toezicht op de uitvoering van) de Wet ondernemingspensioenfondsen BES niet heeft overgenomen.

Worries about growing inequality between citizens and officials on the islands and in European Netherlands, asks for transparent legal justification, raises international-law (self-determination, human rights) concerns, and questions many open delegations to ministerial regulation, the private pension fund structure, and missing protections for members and creditors.
In response to the adjustment proposals, they ask the government for a transparent legal justification for two different kinds of citizens and officials in one country.
Zij vragen de regering naar aanleiding van de aanpassingsvoorstellen om een transparante juridische legitimering voor twee verschillende soorten burgers en bestuurders in één land.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on the Third Amendment Act for the public bodies Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, supporting its aims but raising objections on the Rijksvertegenwoordiger's pension and tax regime, entry into homes without required formalities, the lack of detail on administrative fines by DNB, and the broad power to test for drugs in drink-driving cases. The government's reply (nader rapport) largely followed the advice: it aligned the pension regime with the Dutch European part, added the legitimation and purpose requirement, listed the offences subject to fines, and narrowed the testing powers to breath, blood, urine and saliva.
concerns: The broad power to examine 'other human material' for drink or drug driving restricts bodily integrity and must be concretely limited, which the government did by specifying breath, blood, urine and saliva.
The administrative fine regime lacks specification of violations and addressees, and the legality principle requires more detailed procedural rules, which the government added to the Pensioenwet BES.
Entry into homes without consent lacks the required prior showing of identification and statement of purpose under Article 12 of the Constitution, which the government inserted.

The pension, tax and social security treatment of the former Rijksvertegenwoordiger should be consistently drawn from either the Dutch European part or the BES regime, which the government resolved by choosing the European Dutch regimes.
Numerous redactional remarks on structure, numbering and wording were largely adopted, with a few exceptions explained by the government.

v.summary: The Raad van State advises that the nota van wijziging to the Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba adaptation bill should be partly reconsidered, mainly because it omits notification of special investigative powers and any rule on destruction of data obtained through them, which the Council considers required by Article 13 ECHR and Article 8 ECHR/Article 10 Constitution. The government's nader rapport rejects the notification and destruction duties, citing uniformity with the Antilles and Aruba and administrative burden, but withdraws the criminal procedure provisions from the nota and proposes a ministerial regulation as an emergency measure.
concerns: Absence of a notification duty for special investigative powers may breach the right to an effective remedy under Article 13 ECHR; government points to other routes such as access requests and trial disclosure and a possible directive.

Omission of rules on destruction of data obtained through special investigative powers conflicts with privacy protection under Article 8 ECHR and Article 10 Constitution and the foreseeability requirement; government rejects this for administrative burden and uniformity reasons.
Numerous technical and drafting remarks on article structure, terminology, and placement of amendments; many adopted, others declined for clarity reasons.

32446.s: The bill adds a new chapter 3A to the Wobka giving adoptive parents, on request, a fixed financial contribution toward the costs of intercountry adoption, indexed annually to the consumer price index. The benefit applies to adoptions from 1 January 2009 and requires the request within three years and Dutch nationality acquired by the child.
32446.j: The memorandum explains that the allowance is claimed afterwards so the adoption can be checked, and that the initiative lies with the parent because the central authority and licensed private bodies share the tasks.
q: A separate subsidy decision (art. 4:29 Awb) is not needed, because the allowance is claimed afterwards and it can thus easily be checked whether the adoption has in fact taken place.

Een afzonderlijke beschikking tot subsidieverlening (art. 4:29 Awb) is niet nodig, omdat de tegemoetkoming achteraf wordt aangevraagd en dus eenvoudig kan worden gecontroleerd of de adoptie inderdaad heeft plaatsgevonden.
d: rules on applying for the allowance
annual indexation of the allowance amount

parties: Asks about the rationale for the three-year claim window, the cost items making up adoption expenses, and whether the EU should address intercountry adoption; no check on the executive is raised.
The choice of a three-year period appears somewhat arbitrary.
Het lijkt erop dat de keus voor de termijn van drie jaar enigszins arbitrair is.
Argues the government should contribute more, notes compensation in Norway and Denmark is higher, and asks about cases of weak adoption and whether weak adoptions can be converted.
The compensation amount the government proposes is, according to the PvdA members, not high.
Het compensatie bedrag dat de regering voorstelt, is volgens de leden van de PvdA-fractie niet hoog.
Stresses extreme care in intercountry adoption and suspension of procedures where abuses occur, and asks how eligibility of non-Dutch parents resident in the Netherlands will be checked.
If abuses occur in a certain country, no adoption procedures should take place from that country.
Als er in een bepaald land misstanden plaatsvinden, dienen er geen adoptieprocedures uit dat land plaats te vinden.
Notes the Raad van State finds the motivation for the flat rate unconvincing and asks for a quantified estimate of administrative costs and a differentiation by parental means.
Regarding the chosen flat-rate compensation of EUR 3,700, these members noted that the Council of State does not find the motivation convincing.
In verband met de gemaakte keuze voor een forfaitaire vergoeding van 3700 euro hebben deze leden geconstateerd dat de Raad van State de motivering daarvoor niet overtuigend acht.
Agrees with the Council of State that selection on financial capacity must be avoided, finds the generic scheme insufficient, and asks whether an income-dependent scheme was considered.
They fully agree with the Council of State that selection among prospective adoptive parents on the basis of financial capacity should not take place.
Zij zijn het zeer eens met de opmerking van de Raad van State dat het niet de bedoeling is dat op grond van draagkracht selectie tussen aspirant-adoptiefouders plaatsvindt.
Follows the Council of State in asking for a more convincing motivation of the subsidy scheme, invokes the Commissie Kalsbeek view, and asks why national adoption is not an alternative.
Following the Council of State, they wish to ask the government for a more convincing motivation for the new subsidy scheme.
In navolging van de Raad van State willen zij de regering vragen een overtuigender motivering voor de nieuwe subsidieregeling uit een te zetten.
Sees no reason for further comments on the bill.
At this moment they see no reason to make further comments on this bill.
Zij zien op dit moment geen aanleiding tot het maken van nadere opmerkingen met betrekking tot dit wetsvoorstel.
Welcomes the bill as implementing an earlier parliamentary motion, but asks about cost figures, the 2009-2010 adoption numbers, cost control and the precise reference point for eligibility.
They consider it a good thing that the motion by Van der Vlies et al. on this subject is being implemented.
Zij vinden het een goede zaak dat invulling wordt gegeven aan de motie-Van der Vlies c.s. over dit onderwerp.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised that the draft bill creating a flat-rate allowance for interlandelijke adoption costs was not convincingly justified, since the explanatory memorandum did not give a sound reason for a generic, non-means-tested scheme, and advised a dragende motivering before submission. The minister's reply states that the memorandum was supplemented with a brief justification for choosing a flat-rate amount for all eligible adoptive parents, and the bill was left unchanged.
concerns: The Raad found the motivation for a new subsidy scheme unconvincing, given that the adoption-cost deduction had lapsed and the scheme does not target any demonstrated need or cost type.
The Raad considered that the generic flat-rate scheme, not differentiated by parental means or cost type, does not fit the claimed state responsibility for adoption costs.
The Raad advised including a substantive justification for choosing a flat-rate amount over an income- or cost-dependent scheme, and the explanatory memorandum was supplemented accordingly.

32455.s: The bill adds Article 106a to the Aliens Act 2000 creating a statutory basis for taking a facial image and two fingerprints from third-country nationals, to implement EU Regulation 380/2008 on uniform residence permits. It authorises the Minister, the Minister of Foreign Affairs and designated officials to take the biometrics and allows general administrative orders to set further rules on their application.
32455.j: The memorandum justifies the new power by the need for a national legal basis to take biometrics required by the directly applicable EU regulation, and limits the general administrative order to the manner of taking data for that purpose.
q: These rules may only concern the application of the first paragraph, therefore the manner of taking the biometric characteristics for the intended purpose.
Deze regels kunnen uitsluitend zien op de toepassing van het eerste lid, derhalve op de wijze van afname van de biometrische kenmerken voor het beoogde doel.
d: further rules on application of biometric taking
p: Gives designated ministers and officials power to compulsorily take biometric data from third-country nationals, limited to the purpose of the EU regulation.

parties: Asks whether delegated rules on the practical taking of biometric data may go beyond technical requirements and asks for an example of when such rules would be needed.
Can the government give an example of a situation in which it would be desirable to set further rules?
Kan de regering een voorbeeld noemen van een situatie waarin het wenselijk zou zijn nadere regels te stellen?
Asks how the government has addressed the Council of State's advice on the scope of processing biometric data in the bill and explanatory memorandum.
These members would like to know how the government has incorporated the Council of State's remark on the scope of processing biometric data into the bill and the explanatory memorandum.

Deze leden vernemen graag op welke wijze de regering de opmerking in het advies van de Raad van State over de reikwijdte van het verwerken van biometrische gegevens heeft verwerkt in het wetsvoorstel en in de memorie van toelichting.
Asks about alternative identification for people unable to give fingerprints and why the new biometric requirements do not apply to listed exempt categories.
These members ask why the new biometric requirements do not apply to the listed exempt categories.
Deze leden vragen waarom de nieuwe biometrische eisen niet aan (de verblijfsdocumenten van) de genoemde uitzonderingscategorieën worden gesteld.
Raises concerns about error rates in fingerprints, wrongful entries in the central database, citizens' ability to correct them, and function creep toward a law-enforcement register.
Does the government share these members' concerns that the central database will in practice become a criminal investigation register?
Deelt de regering de zorgen van deze leden dat de centrale database in de praktijk een opsporingsregister zal worden?
Asks for an overview of all purposes for which the fingerprints could be used and for confirmation that there will be no central storage of fingerprints.
They ask the government to provide an overview of all purposes for which the fingerprints, for whose collection this amendment provides a legal basis, could be used.

Zij vragen de regering om een overzicht te verschaffen van alle doeleinden waar de vingerafdrukken – voor de afname waarvan onderhavige wijziging een rechtsgrondslag biedt – voor gebruikt zouden kunnen worden.
Asks how the biometric data will be processed and stored, by which organisation, for what purposes, for how long, and who will have access.
Are the facial image and the two fingerprints stored other than on the residence document?
Worden de gezichtsopname en de twee vingerafdrukken opgeslagen, anders dan op het verblijfsdocument?

v.summary: The Raad van State advises on a bill amending the Vreemdelingenwet 2000 to give a legal basis for taking facial images and two fingerprints for residence permits, supporting its aim but asking that the scope of data processing be narrowed to collection and storage on the permit and that the delegation to lower rules be limited. The government's reply accepts the points on scope and adjusts the bill, but explains that the delegation cannot be limited to purely technical requirements and cannot be excluded for future needs.
concerns: The word 'verwerken' has a broad meaning under the Wet bescherming persoonsgegevens, so the provision should be narrowed to taking and storing the data on the residence document, excluding other uses.
The explanatory memorandum should clarify that the provision does not provide a legal basis for including biometric data in the Visa Information System.

The general delegation for rules on processing biometric data should be limited to technical requirements, but the government says it cannot be confined to purely technical rules and keeps room for practical arrangements.

32464.s: The bill amends the Unemployment Benefits Act, the Sickness Benefits Act and the Work and Income according to Labour Capacity Act to prevent cumulation of sickness benefit duration with unemployment benefit duration, by reducing unemployment benefit duration by sickness benefit received and adjusting income offsetting. It also includes transitional law and a basis for a procedure regulation for employer-less sickness benefit recipients.
32464.j: The memorandum justifies the bill by the need to reduce sickness absence duration; it does not justify any new executive powers.
q: The bill gives the Inspectorate SZW no reason to make comments on supervisability.
Het wetsvoorstel geeft de IWI geen aanleiding tot het maken van opmerkingen over de toezichtbaarheid.
d: Artikel II, onderdeel A / Artikel III, onderdeel A
reference update to provision of WIA on sickness benefit recipients

parties: Asks whether the government will stagger entry into force given UWV remarks and how the re-integration report will be assessed objectively by UWV.
An expert and objective assessment of the re-integration report is of great importance.
Een deskundige en objectieve beoordeling van het re-integratieverslag is van groot belang.
Considers the bill unnecessary and undesirable, based on weak evidence, contrary to the coalition agreement, and creating a two-tier labour market.
They consider this legislation unnecessary and undesirable.
Zij achten deze wetgeving onnodig en ongewenst.
Asks how the bill fits the WW system, which excludes long-term sick people, and how the government will monitor effects on vangnetters.
Does this bill fit within the systematic of the Unemployment Benefits Act?
Past dit wetsvoorstel wel in de wetsystematiek van de Werkloosheidswet?
Questions the assumed misuse of ZW benefits, whether sick people can realistically job-search, and the treatment of different illnesses and pregnancy.
The SP members ask on what basis the government assumes people wrongly claim a ZW benefit.
De leden vragen op basis waarvan de regering veronderstelt dat mensen onterecht aanspraak maken op een ZW uitkering.
Asks when employers learn whether their re-integration efforts suffice and why sick vangnetters lose the earnings-related WGA benefit compared with other workers.
What justifies the difference in treatment between vangnetters and non-vangnetters in this case, these members want to know.
Wat rechtvaardigt het verschil in behandeling van vangnetters en niet-vangnetters in dit geval, zo willen deze leden weten.

32473.s: The bill sets a framework for housing, spatial planning and environmental protection on the public bodies Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, covering building permits, housing allocation, waste, soil, environmental permits and enforcement. Much of the detailed rule-making is delegated to general administrative orders (AMvB), ministerial regulations and island council ordinances, with the Minister of VROM given intervention powers in spatial planning.
32473.j: The memorandum justifies broad delegation to general administrative orders as allowing flexible, gradual introduction of rules suited to conditions on the islands and easy adjustment if implementation proves difficult.
d: binding ministerial instruction to island council on waste rules
general rules and permit categories for establishments
binding conditions set by designated authority
p: Establishes broad executive power via general administrative order to set environmental rules and permit categories for establishments, with the Minister VROM taking over some permit decisions.
Allows the designated authority to set binding conditions that may deviate from the general rules.

parties: Asks about the timing of the overgangstermijn, how best available techniques are assessed, and the scope of interbestuurlijk toezicht and the division of responsibilities between the minister and island councils.
The members of the VVD faction can agree well with this.
De leden van de VVD-fractie kunnen zich daar goed in vinden.
Questions how the islands will have sufficient input into the many AMvBs and ministerial rules to be drafted later, and whether island capacity and consultation are adequate.
To what extent is it guaranteed that the BES islands will have sufficient input in drafting these AMvBs and ministerial regulations?
In hoeverre is gewaarborgd dat de BES-eilanden voldoende inbreng zullen hebben bij het opstellen van deze AMVB’s en ministeriële regelingen?
Asks on what grounds island councils may restrict sale and rental of housing and how transparent and proportionate these measures are.
Finally, these members want to know how it is guaranteed that these measures are applied transparently and proportionately.
Tenslotte willen deze leden weten hoe is gewaarborgd dat deze maatregelen transparant en proportioneel worden ingezet.
Asks how control and enforcement capacity on the islands will be assured and whether budgets for training and capacity are available.
Training of staff is a first requirement, sufficient capacity a second.
Training van medewerkers is een eerste vereiste, voldoende capaciteit een tweede.
Objects to excessive delegation and subdelegation of regulatory power, asks for limitative statutory criteria, and wants the transition deadline set by the House rather than by royal decree.
These members regret this choice because the House of Representatives then has no say over it.
Deze leden betreuren deze keuze omdat de Tweede Kamer er zodoende niets meer over te zeggen heeft.
Asks for involvement of the island council and the Tweede Kamer in lower regulation and for pre- and post-consultation procedures as in the Netherlands.
These members ask what the involvement of the island council and the House of Representatives is in this.
Deze leden vragen wat hierbij de betrokkenheid is van de eilandsraad en de Tweede Kamer.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on the draft Wet VROM BES, which introduces housing, spatial planning and environmental rules for the Caribbean Netherlands islands, and advised simplifying the bill, better justifying sub-delegation, adding medebewind grounds, and reviewing reliance on care-duty provisions. The government's reply largely accepted the advice, adding an evaluation clause, interbestuurlijk toezicht, transitional provisions and textual corrections, while defending the bill's scope and rejecting some points.
concerns: The Raad advised simplifying the bill because a large new legal framework risks harming effectiveness on small islands, but the government largely defended the scope while adding explanation and an evaluation clause.
The Raad objected to the large number of sub-delegations to amvb without justification, and the government revised several delegation provisions and explanations.
The Raad asked for an express statutory basis for medebewind by island councils, which the government said the bill already provides for.
The Raad noted that care-duty provisions lack a shared reference framework on the islands and risk legal uncertainty; the government accepted the concern and committed to education and scholing.
The Raad flagged a gap in transitional law between the end of Dutch Antillean rules and entry into force of the bill, and the government adopted a transitional regulation and transitional articles.
The Raad raised text and terminology inconsistencies and departures from the Wet milieubeheer, which the government largely corrected in the bill and explanatory memorandum.

32527.s: The bill merges the Gooi en Vechtstreek and Flevoland police regions into a new Gooi-Flevoland police region and makes temporary arrangements for its governance, prosecution, personnel, assets, and legal proceedings. It assigns the commissaris van de Koning of Flevoland to act for the new region, with the Noord-Holland commissaris as counterpart, and lets the Minister of Justice designate a Lelystad court for cases from the region.
32527.j: The memorandum justifies the temporary arrangements as needed because the new region spans two provinces and two safety regions, and it treats the merger as a pilot for wider scale enlargement.
q: two commissioners of the King have tasks, powers and responsibilities with respect to one police region
twee commissarissen van de Koningin taken, bevoegdheden en verantwoordelijkheden hebben ten aanzien van één politieregio
d: entry into force by royal decree
value of transferred assets set by minister
list of affected personnel set by minister
minister designates Lelystad court for region's criminal cases
p: The Minister of Justice may decide which court handles criminal cases from the new region, after consulting the judiciary council and prosecutors-general.
The Minister appoints the safety region chair by royal decree after advice from the commissaris van de Koning, a transitional arrangement that alters local appointment routes.

parties: Asks how the merger fits the planned national police structure and what the consequences of the temporary safety-region incongruence will be.
The VVD members note that the congruence between police regions and safety regions will be restored within 5 years.
De leden van de VVD-fractie constateren dat de congruentie van politieregio en de veiligheidsregio’s binnen 5 jaar zal worden hersteld.
Questions the urgency of the merger before the national police structure is clear and asks how the prosecution service will be steered across several arrondissements.
These members see a possible bottleneck in steering the prosecution service in concrete cases, because several arrondissements are involved.
Deze leden zien hierin een mogelijk knelpunt in de aansturing van het OM in concrete zaken, omdat er verschillende arrondissementen betrokken zijn.
Supports a national police reorganised along arrondissement lines and sees temporary arrangements as needless delay; demands a guarantee against further reorganisation costs.
Temporary arrangements like these are, in the PVV's view, of no added value because they can only lead to unnecessary delay.
Tijdelijke voorzieningen als deze zijn in de ogen van de PVV niet van toegevoegde waarde omdat deze alleen maar kunnen leiden tot onnodige vertraging.
Supports consolidation but presses the government on the Raad voor de rechtspraak's objections to the minister's power to direct cases to Lelystad, which it sees as threatening judicial independence.

The provision would offer undesirable influence possibilities that do not fit a state governed by the rule of law, namely impairment of the independence of the judiciary.although it does not word this as its own objection.' ,
De bepaling zou ongewenste beïnvloedingsmogelijkheden bieden die in een rechtsstaat niet passen, namelijk aantasting van de onafhankelijkheid van de rechterlijke macht.
Asks why the Raad voor de rechtspraak was not consulted and whether its unsolicited advice can still be answered; also questions the urgency and the single-CdK arrangement.
Why is there no waiting until the total reorganisation plans for the police are known?
Waarom wordt er niet gewacht tot de totale reorganisatieplannen bij de politie bekend zijn?
Accepts the temporary arrangement but objects that the Raad voor de rechtspraak was not consulted and that ministerial power to allocate cases conflicts with separation of powers.
They consider it important that the execution of operations, such as assigning cases to arrondissements, remains with the court boards themselves and not with the minister..
Zij vinden het van belang dat de uitvoering van de bedrijfsvoering, zoals het toekennen van zaken aan arrondissementen, bij de gerechtsbesturen zelf blijft liggen en niet bij de minister.
Asks how the merger contributes to future-proof quality and what it means for police access, presence in villages and response times.
The mere fact that regions are merged does not by definition make the new region future-proof.
Het enkele feit dat regio’s worden samengevoegd, maakt de nieuwe regio niet per definitie toekomstbestendig.
Asks how local authorities will stay involved, what geographic barriers mean for response times, and why no short consultation round was held.
How is it prevented that the involvement of the local authorities is weakened?
Hoe wordt voorkomen dat de betrokkenheid van de lokale besturen wordt verzwakt?

32536.s: The bill approves for the Netherlands the 2010 tax treaty with Switzerland on avoiding double taxation of income, together with its Protocol, as required under article 91(1) of the Constitution. It enters into force the day after publication in the Staatsblad.
q: The tax treaty between the Kingdom of the Netherlands and the Swiss Confederation to avoid double taxation on income, with Protocol, signed at The Hague on 26 February 2010, requires approval by the States General under article 91(1) of the Constitution.

Het op 26 februari 2010 te ’s-Gravenhage tot stand gekomen Verdrag tussen het Koninkrijk der Nederlanden en de Zwitserse Bondsstaat tot het vermijden van dubbele belasting met betrekking tot belastingen naar het inkomen, met Protocol, ingevolge artikel 91, eerste lid, van de Grondwet de goedkeuring van de Staten-Generaal behoeft

parties: Asks how broadly the mutual agreement procedure and the treatment of dividends under article 10(9) should be read.
The VVD members, following comments from the Dutch Order of Tax Advisers, ask how article 10(9) should be read, i.e. which rate applies.

De leden van de VVD-fractie vragen zich naar aanleiding van de opmerkingen van de Nederlandse Orde van Belastingadviseurs af, hoe artikel 10, negende lid, moet worden gelezen, dus welk tarief is van toepassing?
Asks for clear criteria on 'fishing expeditions' and what counts as a sufficient suspicion for information requests.
Can the government explain exactly what is understood by fishing expeditions, the PvdA members ask. Are there clear criteria for this?
Kan de regering uitleggen wat precies onder fishing expeditions verstaan wordt, zo vragen de leden van de PvdA-fractie. Zijn daar duidelijke criteria voor?
Asks the government to explain the balance of the treaty, which deviates from the OECD model and Dutch treaty policy, and to discuss the policy note with parliament.
The CDA members also note that on a large number of articles Swiss demands have been accepted, so that the treaty departs from the OECD model and Dutch treaty policy.
Voorts willen de leden van de CDA-fractie nog de opmerking maken dat het hen opvalt dat ten aanzien van een groot aantal artikelen van het verdrag bepaalde Zwitserse eisen zijn ingewilligd
Questions the 'fair share' concept, refusals of information requests, budget effects, and sanctions against non-cooperating jurisdictions, demanding more explanation.
A request may not be refused solely because the requested state has no interest in the information or because of bank secrecy.
Een verzoek mag niet geweigerd worden enkel omdat de aangezochte staat zelf geen belang heeft bij de gevraagde informatie of vanwege een bankgeheim
Criticises that the treaty does not cover wealth taxes and that information requests are limited to what is foreseeably relevant, asking who decides relevance.
The Netherlands will only be able to obtain information on request when a request is 'foreseeably relevant'. The first question is who determines whether a request is foreseeably relevant.

Nederland zal alleen «op verzoek» informatie kunnen krijgen wanneer een verzoek «voorzienbaar relevant» is. De eerste vraag die daarbij opkomt is wie bepaalt of een verzoek «voorzienbaar relevant» is?
Asks about the absence of a provision on collection of tax debts and how firm Switzerland's commitment is, and about allocation of powers for hybrid entities.
No provision on the collection of tax debts is included in the treaty, the PVV members note.
Er is geen bepaling ten aanzien van de invordering van belastingschulden in het verdrag opgenomen, aldus de leden van de fractie van de PVV.

v.summary: The Raad van State advises on a bill approving the 2010 Dutch-Swiss tax treaty to avoid double taxation, supporting its aim but raising points on hybrid entities, residence of ship dwellers, dividend exemption for non-business bodies, capital gains on real estate, directors' fees, foreign permanent establishment relief, mutual agreement procedure, and several explanatory gaps. The government's reply (nader rapport) states it adopted the advice by adding examples and clarifications to the explanatory memorandum on each point.
concerns: Explanatory memorandum on hybrid entities should add more examples to clarify the complex treaty provisions.
Application of the treaty to persons living on ships whose home port is in a third state is not secured and should be explained.
Dividend withholding exemption wording excludes non-business bodies, conflicting with Dutch treaty policy; the explanatory memorandum should address them.
The capital gains clause departs from the OECD model by covering real estate in third states; the deviation should be explained.
The definition of director in the directors' fees article should be concretized in the explanatory memorandum.
Relief method for foreign permanent establishments differs from current policy and the relation between treaty and national relief methods is unclear; the explanatory memorandum should clarify both.
The mutual agreement procedure explanation refers to another treaty and should be written out to be self-contained.

32554.s: The bill amends the Police Data Act and the Judicial and Criminal Procedure Data Act to implement EU framework decision 2008/977/JHA on data protection in police and judicial cooperation. It tightens rules on onward transfer to third countries and international bodies, data subject rights, security, and the consultation and enforcement powers of the data protection authority.
32554.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations as needed to implement the EU framework decision's requirements on transfers, designated EU bodies and data processing rules.
q: The framework decision requires supplementing the powers of the Data Protection Authority in this area.
Het kaderbesluit noodzaakt tot aanvulling van de bevoegdheden van het CBP op dit gebied.
d: Designation of EU bodies and rules on transfer and onward use of police and justice data
Further rules on transfer, conditions of use by recipients, and receipt of data from abroad
Designation of EU support body receiving prosecution data
Definition of judicial data to be specified by decree
p: Grounds for refusing police data access are reworded in a way that broadens the police's discretion to withhold information from data subjects, though grounds are listed.
Prosecutors may withhold notification of data processing to data subjects on listed grounds such as preventing obstruction of proceedings and state security.
I.F and II.E (Art. 25 WPG; Art. 18 WJSG)
Response periods for access requests are extended, from four to six weeks for police data and to four weeks for justice data, with possible postponement.
Access to justice data is limited to staff under the Minister and certain Data Protection Act provisions are applied by reference, with no clear new citizen protections added beyond existing ones.
I.J and II.H (Art. 35(4) WPG; Art. 27(3) WJSG)
The Data Protection Authority must be consulted before processing sensitive data or creating high-risk new databases, strengthening an oversight body.
The Data Protection Authority is empowered to impose administrative fines on controllers for breaches of retention and reporting duties, with appeal to the administrative court available.

parties: Asks whether the government has more detail on the planned EU-wide revision of the data protection framework and its timeline, and how the Cbp's powers to act in court are reconciled with the explanatory memorandum.
The VVD members want to know whether the government already has more insight into the details of the proposed revision of the entire European legal framework, including the timeline.
De leden van de VVD-fractie willen weten of de regering al meer zicht heeft op de details van de voorgestelde herziening van het gehele Europeesrechtelijke kader, inclusief tijdpad.

Questions the broad purpose-compatibility exception, the transfer of data to third countries and private parties, and whether the data subject should always be asked consent for use for another purpose.
This seems a fairly strict rule that is directly undermined by the possibility of also allowing processing of personal data for another purpose.
Dit lijkt een vrij strikte regel die direct wordt ondergraven door de mogelijkheid om verwerking van persoonsgegevens ook toe te staan voor een ander doel.

Asks whether member states collect data without purpose and whether the Cbp will be burdened with advisory and supervisory tasks, questioning the fit with its enforcement focus; also asks for a fuller substantiation of the claim that police workload will not increase.
Have these members understood correctly that the College bescherming persoonsgegevens (Cbp) will be (partly) tasked with this?
Hebben deze leden het goed begrepen dat het College bescherming persoonsgegevens (Cbp) hiermee (deels) zal worden belast?

Welcomes clearer rules and oversight but asks which court handles appeals against refusals to correct or erase data, how the adequacy of data protection in new member states is checked, and wants the Wob not to circumvent the purpose limits in the Wpg and Wjsg.
The members asking this question wonder, with regard to article 18 of the framework decision, before which court an appeal can be lodged.
De aan het woord zijnde leden vragen met betrekking tot artikel 18 van het kaderbesluit of bij welke rechterlijke instantie beroep kan worden aangetekend.

Supports safeguards but presses whether transfers to third countries and member states are allowed only with adequate protection in practice, whether Dutch authorities can refuse transfers when in doubt, and whether the Cbp has sufficient budget and powers.

The SP members ask whether the government shares the view that exchanging police, judicial and criminal procedure data with EU member states or third countries is only permissible if adequate data protection actually exists in the other country, both in theory and in practice.

De leden van de SP-fractie vragen of de regering de mening deelt dat het uitwisselen van politiële, justitiële en strafvorderlijke gegevens met EU-lidstaten of met derde landen alleen geoorloofd is als er daadwerkelijk, zowel in theorie (wetgeving) als in de praktijk, toereikende gegevensbescherming bestaat in het andere land.

Regards the framework decision as a minimum floor too low for Dutch standards, asks the government to keep pushing for higher protection, asks why the implementation deadline was missed, and wants the Chamber closely involved in the EU revision.
They maintain that view and therefore see implementation of this framework decision as a floor at European level and too low for Dutch regulation.
Zij blijven die mening toegedaan en zien implementatie van onderhavig kaderbesluit dan ook als een ondergrens in Europees verband en te laag voor de Nederlandse regelgeving.
Asks the government to justify the broadening of the purpose limitation for further processing and to substantiate that it fits practical needs.
These members request the government to further explain why this broadening is necessary.
Deze leden verzoeken de regering nader toe te lichten waarom deze verruiming noodzakelijk is.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a bill implementing EU Framework Decision 2008/977/JBZ on data protection in police and judicial cooperation, plus Europol implementation, raising concerns on definitions, the three-year retention period for disclosure data, implementation transparency, and several gaps in safeguards and sanctions. The government's nader rapport accepted most points, notably extending the retention period to four years and adding missing safeguards and powers for the CBP.
concerns: Unclear alignment between Dutch data-protection terminology (WPG, WJSG) and EU terms, now aligned with the Wbp definition of personal data.
A fixed three-year retention period for disclosure data may not strike a fair balance with data subjects' rights; retention extended to four years.
Transposition table and explanatory memorandum insufficiently explain how each Framework Decision provision is implemented.
Obligation for the controller to shield data independently, not only on request, was missing and has been added.
Procedural safeguards for erasure or periodic review of storage were not clearly implemented and have been added to the table and text.
Criteria for setting the protection level should be laid down in generally binding rules; now placed in the statutory text.
Several redactional remarks on the transposition table and article references were noted.

32617.s: The bill implements in Dutch law the 2007 Hague Convention on international recovery of child support and other family maintenance and the 2007 Hague Protocol on applicable law, together with EU Regulation 4/2009 on maintenance obligations. It designates the Landelijk Bureau Inning Onderhoudsbijdragen as central authority and sets out court procedures for recognition and enforcement of maintenance decisions, including appeals to the Hoge Raad.
