Whether a suspected straw man should lead to refusal of the business relationship under Article 5 was clarified in the explanatory memorandum.
The legal basis in the Third Anti-Money Laundering Directive for the exemption from enhanced client due diligence was unclear, and the exemption was limited to obligations outside the Directive.
The scope of linking FIU register data with other personal data collections needed more explanation in the explanatory memorandum, which was supplemented.
A redactional remark recommended deleting the proposed mandate provision in Article 14(4) Wwft as superfluous given Article 12(3).

33247.s: The bill sets out how the Netherlands assists the European Commission in on-the-spot controls and verifications under EU Regulation 2185/96 against fraud affecting EU financial interests. It designates the Minister of Finance as the contact authority, assigns assisting ministers, and gives designated officials inspection powers and cooperation duties under the General Administrative Law Act.
33247.j: The memorandum justifies the powers by the Commission's need for effective, efficient on-the-spot controls against fraud, and points to the existing Awb supervision framework as a proven standard.
d: designation of competent ministers and officials to assist Commission inspections
p: Designated officials gain access, information and inspection powers over market participants by reference to the Awb supervision provisions, subject to a duty to identify themselves.

parties: Asks how the EU checks relate to existing national control bodies and whether they risk stacking controls and administrative burden on businesses.
Does the EU control take place on the basis of trust, or is there a risk of stacking controls and thereby administrative burdens for entrepreneurs?
Vindt de controle vanuit de EU plaats op basis van vertrouwen, of is er een risico voor een stapeling van controles en daarmee administratieve lasten voor ondernemers?
Objects to transferring national supervisory powers to the EU by regulation, questioning the Commission's legitimacy and the legal basis of the bill, which it deems unlawful.
Transferring national supervisory powers merely by regulation therefore does not make sense in light of the above.
Het op grond van louter een verordening overdragen van nationale toezichtbevoegdheden ligt in het licht van het bovenstaande dan ook niet in de rede.
Asks about sanctions for member states and market participants who fail to cooperate with audits and the powers of officials, to ensure compliance.
Are there sanctions for market participants who do not fully cooperate with the European Commission or a designated official?
Bestaan er sancties voor marktdeelnemers welke niet alle medewerking verlenen aan de Europese Commissie of een aangewezen functionaris?

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division supports the bill implementing EU Regulation 2185/96 on Commission on-the-spot checks against fraud, but asks for clarification of its scope with sectoral EU rules and for replacing the term 'hulp' with 'bijstand'. The government's reply accepts most drafting points, adds clarifications to the explanatory memorandum, and rejects one redactional comment on referring to Regulation 1073/1999.
concerns: The term 'hulp' should be replaced by 'bijstand' to match the regulation's terminology, which was adopted.
The explanatory memorandum should clarify how the regulation relates to sectoral EU rules and which investigations fall within scope.
Several redactional comments on article wording and references were adopted, while the suggestion to add a reference to Regulation 1073/1999 in article 1(b) was not.

33280-V.s: This bill amends the 2012 departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (V) by adjusting commitment and spending figures across policy articles, as part of the spring budget review. It sets the statement in thousands of euros and makes the amended statement effective from 1 June 2012, with retroactive effect if published later.
33280-V.j: The memorandum justifies the budget changes by reference to the Rijksbegrotingsvoorschriften and the Comptabiliteitswet 2001, and explains that commitments for education and global health funds were entered into in 2011, so the 2012 budget is reduced.
q: This is mainly caused by the fact that the planned commitments for the Global Programme for Education and the Global Fund to fight Aids, Tuberculosis and Malaria were entered into in 2011.
Dit wordt hoofdzakelijk veroorzaakt doordat de geplande verplichtingen voor het Global Programme for Education en het Global Fund to fight Aids, Tuberculoses and Malaria in 2011 zijn aangegaan.

33319.s: The bill approves for the European part of the Netherlands the Treaty on Stability, Coordination and Governance in the Economic and Monetary Union, signed in Brussels on 2 March 2012. The treaty requires a structural budget balance rule in national law, with an enforcement role for the European Commission and the Court of Justice.
33319.j: The memorandum justifies the treaty as a structural response to the eurocrisis, arguing that stricter independent supervision and enforcement of budget discipline is necessary given how interwoven member states' finances are.
q: The Netherlands therefore advocates more effectively enforcing existing agreements through strict and independent control over, and enforcement of, the existing agreements.
Nederland pleit daarom voor het effectiever afdwingen van bestaande afspraken, door strenge en onafhankelijke controle op, en handhaving van de bestaande afspraken.
p: Approval of the treaty binds the Netherlands to EU-level budget enforcement, including Commission and Court of Justice oversight of national budget rules, reducing national parliamentary control over fiscal policy.

parties: Asks whether the balance between EU intervention and national policy freedom ('elkaar de maat nemen, niet de wet voorschrijven') is sufficiently respected.
As long as a member state has normal public finances and is in a healthy economic situation, it has a large degree of freedom to make political policy trade-offs.
Zolang een lidstaat een normale overheidshuishouding heeft en in een gezonde economische situatie verkeert, heeft een lidstaat een grote mate van vrijheid om politieke beleidsafwegingen te maken.
Critical of placing the treaty outside the EU legal order, which undermines institutional transparency and the authority of EU decision procedures.
In the view of the PvdA members, this does not benefit institutional transparency in the European Union.
Naar de mening van de leden van de PvdA-fractie komt dit de institutionele transparantie in de Europese Unie niet ten goede.
Asks for a detailed description of the automatic correction mechanism and the sanctions attached to non-compliance with recommendations.
Can this mechanism be described in detail? To what extent does this mechanism differ from the existing sanction mechanisms?
Kan dit mechanisme uitvoerig worden beschreven? In hoeverre wijkt dit mechanisme af van de reeds bestaande sanctiemechanismen?
Objects that the treaty fixes one-sided economic policy that is hard to change democratically, and that recommendations backed by fines lack democratic legitimacy and parliamentary control.
In the view of these members, the treaty leads to fixing a one-sided economic policy that is difficult to change democratically through the treaty.
Het verdrag leidt naar de mening van deze leden tot het vastleggen van een bepaald economisch beleid dat eenzijdig is en door het verdrag lastig op democratische wijze te wijzigen.
Questions whether the new treaty conflicts with EU law and who decides this, and asks how parliament's budget right is guaranteed under a correction mechanism.
EU law has primacy over the new EU treaty, the CDA members note.
Het recht van de Europese Unie heeft voorrang op het nieuwe EU-verdrag, zo lezen de leden van de CDA-fractie.
Supports the treaty but stresses the importance of democratic control by national parliaments and the European Parliament and prefers an eventual amendment of the Functioning Treaty.
The D66 members consider democratic control to be of great importance.
De leden van de fractie van D66 achten de democratische controle van groot belang.
Asks for options for an independent national monitoring body besides the CPB, with defined powers to counterbalance the government, and clarity on sanctions.
These members also ask what powers such a body will have and how it can be ensured that it provides sufficient counterweight to the government.
Daarnaast vragen deze leden welke bevoegdheden een dergelijk orgaan zal krijgen en hoe kan worden geborgd dat een dergelijk orgaan voldoende tegenwicht kan bieden aan de regering.

Asks whether the coordination and convergence measures conflict with the stated freedom of member states to make policy choices, and whether the Council of State's critical remarks on integration are addressed.

At the same time, in the context of coordination and convergence of economic policy, measures are taken that may affect the legislation of individual member states. Is this not contradictory, the SGP members ask.

Tegelijkertijd worden er in het kader van de coördinatie en de convergentie van het economisch beleid maatregelen genomen die impact kunnen hebben op de wetgeving van individuele lidstaten. Is dit niet strijdig met elkaar, zo vragen de leden van de SGP-fractie?

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports the Stabiliteitsverdrag (fiscal compact treaty) as an important part of the eurozone stabilisation strategy but raises critical remarks: overlap with EU law, possible tension with EU institutions' powers under Article 121 TFEU and Article 126 TFEU via Article 7, the parliamentary-legitimacy reasoning, entry-into-force, and budgetary implications. The government's reply (nader rapport) largely accepts the remarks, adds clarifications and amends the explanatory memorandum, but defends the choice of a treaty and the voting-procedure mechanism.
concerns: The Afdeling finds overlap between the treaty and existing EU law, risking dilution of existing EU obligations, and asks for explanation of what the treaty adds to the TFEU and the revised Stability and Growth Pact; the government explains the overlap is procedural and defends the treaty choice while adding explanatory text.

The Afdeling considers that the treaty's Title IV arrangements must be carried out within the EU institutional framework to avoid tension with the powers of EU institutions, notably Article 7 versus Article 126 TFEU; the government agrees on the principle and supplements the memorandum but disputes that Article 7 amends the TFEU.
The Afdeling advises deleting the passage on enhanced national involvement and stronger democratic legitimacy of the treaty, since parliaments can only approve or reject treaties; this was followed.

The Afdeling questions the entry-into-force provision in Article 14, noting that it may reduce pressure on states to ratify given that full eurozone participation is needed; the government replies that linkage to ESM financial assistance maintains ratification pressure and adds clarification.

The Afdeling advises nuancing the statement that the treaty has no budgetary consequences and explaining Article 3(2) on automatic correction mechanisms and parliamentary prerogatives; the explanatory memorandum was adjusted accordingly.

33346.s: The bill extends the recidivism rule for serious traffic offences to driving under the influence of drugs, and raises the age at which older driving licence holders must be re-examined from 60 to 65 and from 65 to 70. It also makes related technical amendments to the Wegenverkeerswet 1994 and sets transitional and commencement rules.
33346.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation by stating that the drug thresholds will be set by general administrative order for the substances the Netherlands Forensic Institute has detected in drivers' blood, with article 8(1) serving as a fallback for new drugs.
q: Above those threshold values, which will be designated by general administrative order, driving or causing a vehicle to be driven under the influence of drugs is punishable.
Boven die grenswaarden die bij algemene maatregel van bestuur zullen worden aangewezen, is het besturen of doen besturen van een voertuig onder invloed van drugs strafbaar.
d: I, onderdeel A (art. 8, vijfde lid, Wegenverkeerswet 1994)
drug concentration thresholds for driving under the influence

parties: Asks for the consequences of the bill to be known before it is debated and questions whether the age-test review's effects on road safety are adequately considered.
The VVD members ask whether this is the right order, since they are now debating the bill and must be able to oversee its consequences.

De leden van de VVD-fractie vragen of dit wel de juiste volgorde is, aangezien de leden van de VVD-fractie nu het wetsvoorstel behandelen en moeten kunnen overzien wat de consequenties van dit wetsvoorstel zijn.
Supports the bill's aims but questions the added value of warning letters, asks for alternatives, and wants the age-test changes handled fairly for older drivers.
The PvdA members do ask, however, what the added value of a letter for this is.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie vragen echter wel wat de meerwaarde van een brief hiervoor is.
Asks how the government will deal with drugs that are not detectable but can still affect driving ability.
The PVV members ask how the government will deal with drugs that are not detectable but nevertheless can have an effect on the driving ability of the driver.
De leden van de PVV-fractie vragen op welke manier de regering om zal gaan met drugs die niet waarneembaar zijn, maar weldegelijk hun uitwerking kunnen hebben op de rijvaardigheden van de bestuurder.
Questions whether the alcohol lock programme is still necessary and asks why the age-based test is not abolished at once rather than through further review.
The SP members ask why this cannot be arranged all at once.
De leden van de SP-fractie vragen waarom dit niet in één keer kan worden geregeld.

Supports the drugs recidivism extension but questions why the CJIB rather than the CBR is designated to register licence points, and asks why the law changes before the review of abolishing testing is complete.
The CDA members consider the Central Bureau for Driving Licences (CBR) a more suitable body to carry out this task.
De leden van de CDA-fractie achten het Centraal Bureau voor Rijvaardigheidsbewijzen (CBR) een meer geschikte instantie voor uitvoering van deze taak.
Asks why intoxicant-related convictions are not registered, whether cumulative effects of minor offences can lead to licence invalidity, and how monitoring of the age-limit change will be done.
The D66 members consider it very important to monitor the effects of the bill well, because road safety is paramount for them.
De leden van de D66-fractie vinden het goed monitoren van de effecten van het wetsvoorstel van groot belang, omdat de verkeersveiligheid bij hen voorop staat.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised that a bill extending the recidivism rule for serious traffic offences to drugs and below-limit alcohol offences, and raising the licence check age from 70 to 75, be revised. The minister's reply largely adopted the drafting and technical points, explained the 1.3 per mille threshold and the test of driving capacity, and defended the age increase while announcing further research.
concerns: The Afdeling objected that two different test criteria (1.3 per mille threshold versus inability to drive properly) would apply to materially similar conduct, and advised harmonising the legal consequences.

The Afdeling found the motivation for raising the licence check age from 70 to 75 insufficiently grounded in precise research given road safety risks, and asked for the memorie van toelichting to be supplemented.
The Afdeling advised excluding alcohol offences committed before the act's entry into force from the recidivism rule, as a tightening to the detriment of licence holders.
Technical corrections were made to erroneous cross-references and formulations in the alcohol lock programme rules and elsewhere in the bill.

33355.s: The bill implements EU Directive 2010/64 on interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings by amending the Dutch Code of Criminal Procedure and related laws. It creates a general right for suspects who do not sufficiently understand Dutch to be assisted by an interpreter and to receive written translations of key documents, with the state bearing the cost.
33355.j: The memorandum justifies the new rights by ECHR and EU Charter case law (Kamasinski, Cuscani) and the directive's obligations, and states that the judge as ultimate guardian of a fair trial must check interpretation adequacy.
q: First, a general power is included allowing the suspect to be assisted by an interpreter throughout the entire procedure.
In de eerste plaats is een algemene bevoegdheid van de verdachte opgenomen om zich tijdens de gehele procedure te laten bijstaan door een tolk.

parties: Asks whether victims should also have the right to translated essential documents and whether the government will take measures to give them equal access.
These members ask whether victims of an offence also have the right to translation of essential procedural documents in a language they understand.
Deze leden vragen of slachtoffers van een misdrijf ook recht op vertaling van essentiële processtukken in een voor hun begrijpelijke taal.

Asks who decides which documents are not relevant enough to translate and whether the accused is informed in time to object, and notes disagreement with the judiciary and bar on the scope of essential documents.
Who decides in the first instance when certain documents are not relevant (enough) and therefore need not be translated?
Wie bepaalt in eerste instantie wanneer bepaalde stukken niet relevant (genoeg) zijn en dus niet hoeven worden vertaald?
Opposes EU minimum rules for suspects and argues Dutch law already largely complies, preferring a stronger position for victims.
The members in question stress that they remain opposed to minimum rules for suspects imposed at European level.
De aan het woord zijnde leden benadrukken tegenstander te blijven van minimumregels voor verdachten die in Europees verband worden opgelegd.

Argues the translation right is too narrowly drawn by limiting it to essential documents, asks why the whole file is not translated, and asks how disputes over essential documents are resolved; also concerned about interpreter quality and tendering.
The SP members ask whether the right to translation is not drawn too narrowly, now that the choice has been made in principle to translate only essential procedural documents.
De leden van de SP-fractie stellen de vraag of het recht op vertaling niet te beperkt wordt vastgelegd, nu er voor is gekozen in beginsel slechts de essentiële processtukken te vertalen.
Welcomes the directive as a step toward a common minimum level of protection for suspects and has no further comments.
These members have noted that the Netherlands already largely complies with what the directive prescribes.
Deze leden hebben geconstateerd dat Nederland reeds grotendeels voldoet aan hetgeen de richtlijn voorschrijft.

Supports minimum rights for suspects but questions the standard restriction on documents for translation, the quality of legal interpreters and translators, the register, the cost and timeliness of translations, and the exception to interpretation in article 23.
These members therefore ask to what extent there will be a difference in treatment between Dutch-speaking suspects and suspects who speak another language.
Deze leden vragen dan ook in hoeverre hier sprake zal zijn van een verschil in behandeling tussen Nederlandstalige verdachten en anderstalige verdachten.

v.summary: The Council of State's Advisory Division supports the bill implementing Directive 2010/64/EU on interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings but raises remarks on administrative penalty orders, detention decisions (including ophouden voor onderzoek), raadkamer hearings, written decisions, identification of interpreter need, changes to the charge, videoconferencing and coordination with the raadsman en politieverhoor bill. The government's reply (nader rapport) accepts several points, such as translating penalty orders for misdemeanours, mondelinge mededeling of detention orders, translation of amended charges and a coordination clause, but rejects others, including a statutory interpreter-identification procedure, translation of raadkamer decisions and a legal basis for videoconferencing.
concerns: Interpreter assistance in raadkamer proceedings should not be excludable where investigation interests are seriously harmed, since the directive contains no such exception; the government disagrees, arguing that the exception only applies where the suspect is not heard at all.

Raadkamer decisions should be translated like judgments under the directive's wording 'any judgment'; the government holds that 'vonnissen' does not cover raadkamer decisions, though a right to request translation under article 32a is available.

A statutory procedure for establishing whether a suspect needs interpreter assistance, with the prosecutor deciding in case of disagreement, should be included in the law; the government prefers implementation through an OM aanwijzing.

Written or oral communication in an understandable language of detention orders, including ophouden voor onderzoek and its extension, must be regulated; the government adds an oral communication rule in article 61.
Translation of an amended tenlastelegging (articles 313-314 Sv) must be provided to a suspect who does not understand Dutch; the government added this to article 314.

Clarify that the translation distinction between misdemeanour and offence penalty orders applies irrespective of the issuing authority, and address the administrative penalty order; the government clarified this in the explanatory memorandum.

Videoconferencing for interpreting needs a legal basis implementing article 2(6) of the directive; the government considers regulation premature and points to future review and the interpreter-phone guidance.
A coordination clause with the raadsman en politieverhoor bill should be included; the government will include it in whichever bill is submitted last.

33364.s: The bill amends the Aliens Act 2000 to implement EU Directive 2010/65 on electronic reporting formalities for ships arriving in or departing from EU ports. It adds crew data to passenger data reporting and allows deviation from the General Administrative Law Act's requirement on paper-based or non-electronic submissions where needed for implementing a treaty or binding EU act.
33364.j: The memorandum justifies the deviation as needed to implement the EU directive's deadline for electronic submission and to enable a single maritime electronic window.
q: In doing so, in implementation of a treaty or a binding EU legal act, deviation from article 2:13, first paragraph, of the General Administrative Law Act may be permitted.
Daarbij kan ter uitvoering van een verdrag of een bindende EU-rechtshandeling worden afgeweken van artikel 2:13, eerste lid, van de Algemene wet bestuursrecht.
d: Artikel I, onderdeel 2 (art. 4, vierde lid, Vw 2000)
detailed rules on electronic reporting of passenger and crew data
p: Artikel I, onderdeel 2 (art. 4, vierde lid, Vw 2000)

Allows rules implementing the reporting duty to depart from the general requirement in art. 2:13(1) Awb, reducing a procedural protection for those submitting information, though limited to treaty or EU-law implementation.

parties: Asks how other member states implement the EU proposal, what costs and savings arise, whether national add-ons remain, and how domestic data exchange changes.
The VVD members ask whether, in implementing the directive in the Netherlands, there are still so-called national add-ons and, if so, which ones.
De leden van de VVD-fractie vragen of bij de implementatie van de richtlijn in Nederland nog sprake is van zogenaamde «nationale koppen» en zo ja, welke koppen dat in dat geval zijn.

Questions the necessity of collecting crew data, the consequences of electronic-only reporting when systems fail, the sharing of data with other authorities, privacy and hacking risks, and possible use for immigration enforcement and criminal investigation.
The SP members want to prevent passengers and crew members from being treated as criminals in advance.},
De leden van de SP-fractie willen voorkomen dat passagiers en bemanningsleden bij voorbaat als crimineel worden gezien.

33409.s: The bill amends the 2012 departmental budget of the Ministry of Finance (IXB), mainly to reflect an increase in the capital of the European Investment Bank, by altering budget amounts in thousands of euros and setting its entry into force. It contains no delegation of rule-making power, no new executive discretion, and no oversight or review provisions.
q: is amended, as appears from the relevant budget statement attached to this law
wordt gewijzigd, zoals blijkt uit de desbetreffende bij deze wet behorende staat

33427.s: The bill allows criminal and administrative sanctions to be enforced directly on English-language treaty texts and international standards referred to in Dutch statutes (Arbeidstijdenwet, Kernenergiewet, Luchtvaartwet, Scheepvaartverkeerswet, Telecommunicatiewet, Warenwet, Wet luchtvaart, Wet voorkoming verontreiniging door schepen), without a Dutch translation. It is justified as an exception to the Dutch-language requirement implied by the legality principle of Article 16 of the Constitution.
33427.j: The memorandum justifies the change by the open economy and the fact that professionals already work with the English authentic text, and by avoiding confusion from discrepancies between translation and original, while acknowledging exceptional nature and tight limits.
q: In those – exceptional – cases it is justified that enforcement, through criminal prosecution or an administrative fine, may also take place on the basis of the original language version.
In die – uitzonderlijke – gevallen is het gerechtvaardigd dat ook de handhaving, via een strafvervolging of een bestuurlijke boete, kan geschieden op basis van de originele taalversie.
d: alternative effective date for AETR amendments
p: ARTIKEL I B and C; ARTIKEL II-VIII (new art. 82, 75a, 15.3a, 13b, 11.28, 37b and amendment of art. 31 Scheepvaartverkeerswet)

Enforcement and sanctioning may rest directly on English-language international texts that have not been officially translated into Dutch, reducing citizens' ability to know the rules that can be punished, though limited to listed statutes and to published texts.

parties: Accepts limited use of English only where the sector already uses it and translation is technically impossible, but insists that citizens must know what conduct is punishable and that the accused can defend themselves.
If a criminal case arises, the suspect must know what he is accused of and what he must defend against.
Als het tot een strafzaak komt, dient de verdachte te weten waarvan hij wordt beschuldigd en waartegen hij zich dient te verweren.

Asks the government to justify the exception to the legality principle and whether current law creates structural legal uncertainty, and whether the exception will extend to other languages or sectors.
They therefore ask whether current legislation poses a structural problem regarding legal uncertainty and enforcement, such that an exception to the legality principle is justified.

Zij vragen dan ook of de huidige wetgeving een structureel probleem oplevert voor wat betreft rechtsonzekerheid en handhaving, waardoor het gerechtvaardigd is een uitzondering op het legaliteitsbeginsel te maken.
Insists the exception must remain exceptional, questions the savings argument, and asks whether accused persons who do not understand English can receive a fair trial under Article 6 ECHR.
These members stress that it must remain an exception. The main rule must be that criminal provisions are in Dutch.
Deze leden benadrukken dat het bij uitzonderingen moet blijven. De hoofdregel moet zijn dat strafbepalingen in het Nederlands zijn.

Asks how foreseeability is guaranteed when reliance on English-language rules may require specialist knowledge, and whether oral translation by the prosecutor creates risks of interpretation differences.
These members ask the government how it intends to prevent foreseeability being guaranteed only for specialists or after extensive consultation.
Deze leden vragen de regering hoe zij probeert te voorkomen dat de voorzienbaarheid enkel voor specialisten of na uitgebreide consultatie gewaarborgd is.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised that the bill allowing criminally enforceable provisions in English without Dutch translation was insufficiently justified, as the Hoge Raad's 1997 interpretation of Article 16 of the Constitution would be abandoned without a convincing necessity, and that the exception criteria should be narrowed and defined in the Criminal Code. The minister's reply largely accepted the remarks by sharpening the justification, clarifying cost is not a criterion, narrowing the scheepvaart and arbeidstijden provisions, and explaining prosecution implications, but declined to move the exception criteria into the Criminal Code.
concerns: Departure from the Hoge Raad's interpretation of Article 16 of the Constitution requires a substantive justification of necessity, which the government strengthened without fully rejecting the need for the change.
Enforceability of criminal provisions only in English raises concerns about determinability of criminal norms, which the government addressed only by explaining why risks are limited.

Articles IV and VIII allowed virtually any decision of international organisations to be designated as criminal through lower regulation; the government narrowed the scope to specific IMO and AETR instruments but did not add the criteria to the Criminal Code.
Cost of translation was unclear as a justification; the government clarified it is not a standalone criterion and that savings are a side effect.
Implications for prosecution and charging in English were not addressed; the government added explanation and an example.
Redactional remarks and the terminology change from economisch delict to strafbaar feit were incorporated.

33436.s: The bill amends the Leegstandwet to extend the maximum period of temporary letting of vacant dwellings, from up to two years (renewable) to a maximum of ten years for buildings, five or seven years for other categories, and removes the municipality's discretion to refuse such permits where specified conditions are met. It also removes the Crisis- en herstelwet provision 2.8 and disapplies certain Civil Code tenancy protections for these dwellings.
33436.j: The memorandum justifies the extended period and removal of discretion by the current stagnation in the housing market and the need to make investments in temporary letting worthwhile for owners.
q: The cabinet proposes extending the maximum period of temporary letting for the category of dwellings in a building to ten years, in order to offer more opportunities to make these investments profitable.

Het kabinet stelt voor de maximale termijn van tijdelijke verhuur voor de categorie woonruimte in een gebouw te verlengen tot tien jaren, teneinde meer mogelijkheden te bieden deze investeringen lonend te maken.
p: Artikel I, onderdeel A, punt 2 (artikel 15, vierde lid)
Municipal mayors and aldermen may refuse a temporary letting permit only on the statutory grounds, removing their discretion to attach further local conditions to such permits.
Artikel I, onderdeel A, punt 3 (artikel 15, vijfde lid)
Permit duration is extended up to ten years with renewals, a longer period in which temporary letting is permitted with limited tenant protection.
Artikel I, onderdeel B, punt 1 (artikel 16, eerste en tweede lid)

Civil Code rent-price protections and the possibility of referring disputes to the rent commission are disapplied for these temporarily let dwellings, reducing citizens' legal protection against the state-authorised letting arrangement.
Repeal of article 2.8 of the Crisis- en herstelwet removes a provision of that law, altering the framework for municipal decisions on vacant dwellings.

parties: Asks why the permit requirement was not abolished in favour of a notification duty and questions the scope of municipal discretion, pushing for less administrative burden and greater leeway for owners.
After all, that saves the homeowner administrative hassle and money.
Dat scheelt de huizenbezitter immers administratieve rompslomp en geld.

Worries that releasing rent protection for temporary tenants and the seven-year maximum term could enable profiteering and price increases, and that municipalities should be allowed additional conditions.
As the present bill is designed and justified, the PvdA members remain concerned that this legislation could facilitate landlord profiteering and abuse.
Zoals het voorliggende wetsvoorstel nu is vormgegeven en gemotiveerd, blijft bij de leden van de PvdA-fractie de zorg bestaan dat deze wetgeving huisjesmelken en misbruik in de hand kan helpen.
Agrees with the government on the bill's usefulness for reducing double housing costs and fighting squatting.
It is also a good tool in the continuous and appreciated fight against squatters, the PVV members state.
Ook is het een goed middel in de continue en gewaardeerde strijd tegen het krakerstuig, zo stellen de leden van de PVV-fractie.
Questions the removal of tenant rights and the reliance on municipal discretion against abuse, and asks for data on enforcement and evaluation of the Wet kraken en leegstand.
It seems that the temporary tenant is thereby made outlaw-like.
Het lijkt erop dat hiermee de tijdelijke huurder vogelvrij wordt.
Welcomes the bill but notes it is a temporary solution requiring structural measures; no further questions.
These members do see that the present bill offers a temporary solution where ultimately structural measures are needed.
Deze leden zien wel dat het voorliggende wetsvoorstel een tijdelijke oplossing biedt waar er uiteindelijk structurele maatregelen nodig zijn.

Asks whether temporary tenants could be forced to move through termination or rent increases and whether notice periods should be proportionate, and asks about follow-up on a motion for broader consultation.
These members ask whether this bill makes it possible for these temporary tenants to be forced to move through termination of the lease or a sharp rent increase.
Deze leden vragen of het met dit wetsvoorstel mogelijk is dat deze tijdelijke huurders door opzegging van het huurcontract of een forse stijging van de huur gedwongen kunnen worden te verhuizen.
Supports loosening the Leegstandswet regime and asks how the changes relate to its original purpose and how the five-year interval and six-month minimum term are justified.

33472.s: The bill strengthens quality assurance in Dutch higher education by tightening the accreditation system, creating risk-based inspection of higher education institutions for a temporary period, and requiring external members on examination boards at universities. It also gives the Minister of Education a power to issue binding directions (aanwijzing) to supervisory boards of higher education and vocational institutions in cases of mismanagement, after an inspection investigation.
33472.j: The memorandum justifies the new powers by pointing to inspection and NVAO findings that existing internal and external safeguards failed to detect quality problems, and to the government's constitutional responsibility for education; it also says the powers are limited to ultimum remedium use.
q: The inspection report will need to contain serious conclusions on one or more of the listed elements of mismanagement before the directive power is used.
Het Inspectierapport zal zware conclusies moeten bevatten over één of meer van genoemde elementen van wanbeheer alvorens sprake is van inzet van de aanwijzingsbevoegdheid.
d: Artikel I, R (art. 9.9a WHW) and T (art. 10.3e WHW), U (art. 11.7a WHW)
minister's binding directions to supervisory boards for mismanagement
minister may unilaterally change expiry dates of existing accreditation decisions
Artikel I, E (art. 5a.8 WHW, derde lid) and Artikel I, J/K (art. 5a.13d/13e)
NVAO appoints expert committees and forms visitation groups
minister may extend accreditation term by up to two years
Artikel III, F (art. 12a WOT, lid 3 en 4)
inspectorate may conduct risk-based investigations under conditions set by the Minister
investigations on minister's direction or inspectorate's own initiative under conditions set by the Minister
royal decree may change the 2017 date of the sunset/entry into force for risk-based inspection
p: Minister may issue binding directions to supervisory boards of institutions for mismanagement, subject to a prior inspection investigation, a report, four weeks for the board to respond, and appeal to the administrative court.

Inspectorate may on its own initiative investigate higher education institutions where serious risks are identified, under conditions set by the Minister, subject to proportionality and a planned four-year evaluation.
Artikel I, E, H, J (art. 5a.2, 5a.8, 5a.13d WHW)
NVAO is given the power to appoint expert committees and form visitation groups, with students included on committees and an appeal route available.
Minister may once change expiry dates of existing accreditation and new programme decisions to align visitation groups.
Artikel I, F (art. 5a.9, lid 10) and Artikel I, H (art. 5a.11, lid 10)
Minister may extend accreditation and programme approval terms by up to two years to allow joint assessment of a visitation group.
Examination boards must include external members and exclude board members or persons with financial responsibility, which strengthens independent checks within institutions.

parties: Asks why the Inspectorate's temporary role and a ministerial instruction power are not created earlier, and how the accreditation panels and NVAO role change in practice.
These members do see reason to ask a few questions.
Deze leden zien wel aanleiding tot het stellen van enkele vragen.
Questions whether the proposal is proportionate and whether the NVAO's enhanced role and the Inspectorate's oversight will work, given the Council of State's doubts.
Of course, the value of diplomas must at all times be prevented from being called into question.
Vanzelfsprekend moet te allen tijden worden voorkomen dat de waarde van diploma’s in twijfel wordt getrokken.
Asks whether the situation amounts to a systemic crisis and which structural flaws could cause problems in academic education.

The members further ask whether, given the seriousness of the established shortcomings and the remark that the existing system of internal and external quality safeguards offers guarantees, there is not a systemic crisis.

De leden van de PVV-fractie vragen of gezien de zwaarte van de vastgestelde tekortkomingen en de opmerking dat het bestaande stelsel van interne en externe kwaliteitswaarborgen garanties biedt er niet sprake is van een systeemcrisis.
Doubts the measures suffice while the governance model and performance-based funding remain unchanged; questions the 'Inspectorate' sanctions that fall on students and staff rather than boards.
They do ask whether the proposed measures are sufficient as long as the underlying causes are not addressed.
Wel stellen zij de vraag of de voorgestelde maatregelen voldoende zijn, zolang de onderliggende oorzaken niet worden aangepakt.
Opposes the bill as lacking necessity and warns against a regulatory reflex; wants evaluation of recent reforms before new legislation and notes the Council of State's objections.
These members warn against the regulatory reflex whereby incidents must immediately lead to more laws and regulations.
Deze leden waarschuwen voor de regelreflex waarbij incidenten direct moeten leiden tot meer wet- en regelgeving.

Questions the necessity of the bill since existing oversight exists and the problem was non-enforcement; prefers horizontal oversight via works councils and programme committees and asks why the bill was not withdrawn.
Like the Council of State's advisory division in its supplementary report, they question the usefulness and necessity of this bill.
Zij zetten vraagtekens, net als de afdeling advisering van de Raad van State in het nader rapport, bij nut en noodzaak van dit wetsvoorstel.
Welcomes the ministerial instruction power and stronger student position but doubts the bill addresses root causes such as funding incentives and expansion culture.
They appreciate the creation of an instruction power and the strengthening of the student's position.
Zij waarderen het creëren van een aanwijzingsbevoegdheid en het versterken van de positie van de student.
Argues there is insufficient reason for new legislation, since the failures concerned compliance with existing law, and objects to added regulatory and administrative burden.
In the incidents that occurred, it was found that it is not the law that falls short, but compliance with the current law.
Bij de incidenten die hebben plaatsgevonden, is geconstateerd dat niet de wet tekortschiet, maar de naleving van de huidige wet.

Warns that the bill risks eroding professional responsibility and creates an overreaching state with more external oversight; objects to the ministerial instruction power and asks for evaluation first.
They note that very recently measures have been taken aimed at improving the quality and functioning of higher education.
Zij constateren dat nog zeer recent maatregelen zijn getroffen waarmee beoogd werd de kwaliteit en het functioneren van het hoger onderwijs te verbeteren.
Asks about the consequences of ministerial designation for managers, institutions and students, who may be unfairly hit by funding sanctions, and how long problems can persist before intervention.
The members of this faction fear that it is mainly students and teachers who will be hit by a funding sanction, without this sanction leading to a solution of the identified problems.

De leden van deze fractie vrezen dat het vooral de studenten en docenten zijn die worden geraakt door een bekostigingssanctie, zonder dat deze sanctie leidt tot een oplossing van geconstateerde problemen.

Doubts the necessity of the law, asks for justification with concrete historical examples and a table of designation powers, and argues that designation is ex post and that horizontal oversight should act preventively.
They still have question marks about the usefulness and necessity of this law and therefore have some questions.
Zij zetten nog altijd vraagtekens bij nut en noodzaak van deze wet en hebben daarom enkele vragen.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division advised against the higher education quality assurance bill, questioning its necessity and urgency, objecting to NVAO appointing assessment committees, to risk-based inspectorate oversight and to a ministerial instruction power, and advising against stronger examination committee independence. The government's reply accepted several points (inspectorate remains complementary, clausulation of accreditation extension, dropping the 'kennelijke geest' ground, specifying retention period), but kept the NVAO appointment power in limited form, the risk-based supervision as a temporary measure, the mandatory external member, and the ministerial instruction power.
concerns: The Council questioned the necessity and urgency of the bill given that the problems concern compliance rather than the law itself; the government maintains the bill is necessary but adjusted the explanatory memorandum.

The Council objected that NVAO appointing assessment committees concentrates norm-setting and assessment in one body, undermining institutional primary responsibility; the government narrowed the power with safeguards but kept NVAO appointment.

The Council argued that risk-based inspectorate supervision of quality is ineffective and overlaps with NVAO accreditation; the government kept it as a temporary four-year measure with ministerial conditions.

The Council advised clarifying in the explanatory memorandum how the ministerial instruction power relates to existing sanctions, and limiting it to repeated breaches of funding conditions; the government removed the 'kennelijke geest' ground but kept the power.
The Council noted that sanctioning conduct contrary to the 'spirit' of the law conflicts with legal certainty; the government agreed to remove this ground.

The Council questioned whether enough experts would be available for clustered visitations and whether a mandatory external examination committee member is feasible; the government kept the external member requirement with a delay for universities.
The Council made numerous drafting remarks and corrections to the articles of the WHW and WOT, which the government adopted.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on the third amendment note to the bill strengthening quality safeguards in higher education, which would broaden the minister's instruction power beyond financial-governance mismanagement to cover threats to educational quality. The Raad found the power insufficiently defined, unnecessary given existing supervision tools, and advised reconsideration; the government's reply largely accepts the criticism by narrowing the trigger to breach of the quality-assurance funding condition, adding time limits, and clarifying the ultima ratio character of the instruction.
concerns: The minister's instruction power is nearly unbounded because neither the text nor the explanatory memorandum defines the scope of measures it may require; the government adds a reference to the specific funding condition on quality assurance and a time limit, but does not fully define the scope.

The necessity of the expanded instruction power as an indispensable tool for acute, system-threatening quality problems has not been shown, given existing and proposed financial supervision; the government disagrees, arguing that the Amarantis case showed a gap in intervention options.

An instruction power cannot be used preventively and must be a last resort after other instruments are exhausted; the government stresses procedural safeguards and proportionality requirements but rejects the view that financial supervision suffices.

The power could require content-related educational and policy measures, interfering with institutional autonomy without an adequate legal basis; the government says this is unfounded except for compliance with funding conditions falling under the governing body's quality-assurance task.
Editorial remark that the phrase 'in gevaar' should be added in article I, part B, which the government adopted.

33480-IIB.s: This bill amends the 2012 budget statement of the other High Councils of State and the Governors' cabinets (IIB), adjusting appropriations for items such as the Raad van State, the Algemene Rekenkamer and the National Ombudsman. It is a budgetary adjustment linked to the Najaarsnota, with the changes taking effect from 1 December 2012.
q: Amendment of the 2012 budget statement of the other High Councils of State and the Governors' cabinets (IIB) (amendment linked to the Najaarsnota)
Wijziging van de begrotingsstaat van de overige Hoge Colleges van Staat en de Kabinetten van de Gouverneurs (IIB) voor het jaar 2012 (wijziging samenhangend met de Najaarsnota)

33481.s: The bill changes the financing of the Sociaal-Economische Raad (SER) so that its net operating costs are paid from the Algemeen Werkloosheidsfonds instead of a separate levy under the Handelsregisterwet, and tightens its annual accounts by requiring an accountant's opinion and ministerial approval of the adopted accounts. It also sets a sunset clause, to be reviewed within three years, allowing the law to be terminated by royal decree.
33481.j: The memorandum justifies the financing route by minimising administrative costs now that a separate levy is unnecessary, and says the arrangement will be evaluated within three years.
q: Implementation costs for the SER are minimised with this system, because a separate levy is no longer needed.
De uitvoeringskosten voor de SER worden met deze systematiek geminimaliseerd, omdat nu geen aparte heffing meer nodig is.
d: further rules on financing SER from the unemployment fund
further rules on use of current account funds, with Finance minister
entry into force and termination of the law by royal decree
p: Requires an accountant's opinion on lawful acquisition and spending of funds and ministerial approval of the SER's adopted accounts, adding oversight of the SER's finances by the executive.
Funds SER costs from the general unemployment fund rather than a dedicated levy, reducing parliamentary control over that revenue stream, with a three-year evaluation and sunset clause as safeguards.

parties: Asks whether the AWf is an appropriate instrument for SER financing, and whether SER independence is preserved if financed from general funds.
asks whether, if the financing comes from general funds, the independence of the SER is still guaranteed.
vragen of indien de financiering uit de algemene middelen komt, de onafhankelijkheid van de SER nog is gewaarborgd.
Supports the need for a new financing form for the SER following the reorganisation of the Chambers of Commerce.
support the need, due to the reorganisation of the Chambers of Commerce and the amendment of the Trade Register Act 2007, to arrive at a new form of financing for the Sociaal-Economische Raad (SER).

onderschrijven de noodzaak om vanwege de reorganisatie van de Kamers van Koophandel en de wijziging van de Handelsregisterwet 2007 te komen tot een nieuwe vorm van financiering van de Sociaal Economische Raad (SER).

Objects that financing the SER from the AWf and general funds conflicts with the benefit principle and the purpose of the unemployment premium, and proposes equal thirds funding by government, employers and unions.
These members consider a withdrawal from the AWf for SER costs to be in conflict with the AWf premium as a levy or earmarked tax.
Deze leden achten een uitname uit het Awf voor de SER-kosten in strijd met de Awf-premie als heffing of bestemmingsbelasting.
Asks whether self-employed workers contribute via the entrepreneur allowance and the AWf, and asks for the substantive reasons for the horizon provision.
ask for the government's substantive arguments on the basis of which the proposed amendment could lapse by royal decree.
vragen naar de inhoudelijke argumenten van de regering op basis waarvan de voorgestelde wetswijziging bij koninklijk besluit kan komen te vervallen.

Asks why the financing structure is changed, notes the Council of State's objection to general-budget financing of the SER, and asks whether the government will adopt its advice to have other parties contribute.
financing of the SER from general funds, which would occur in the event of an AWf deficit, does not fit with the intended continuation of the current financing of the SER by business

bekostiging van de SER uit de algemene middelen, waarvan sprake zou zijn bij een tekort in het AWf, zich niet verhoudt met de nagestreefde continuering van de huidige wijze van financiering van de SER door het bedrijfsleven

Asks whether the SER may set its own budget without a maximum, whether comparable institutions have such powers, and what alternatives were considered given critical remarks from the Council of State and UWV.
note that both the Council of State and the Employee Insurance Agency (UWV) raise critical remarks about the policy choice to finance the SER from the AWf.
constateren dat zowel de Raad van State als het Uitvoeringsinstituut werknemersverzekeringen (UWV) kritische kanttekeningen plaatsen bij de beleidsmatige keuze om de SER te financieren uit het Awf.

v.summary: The Raad van State's advisory division advised in August 2012 that the proposed financing of the SER via the Awf (unemployment fund) lacked adequate justification and that a sunset clause should be considered, and that Awf-funding from general revenue was inconsistent with the stated continuity of employer-based financing. The minister's reply of November 2012 expanded the justification, clarified that no fundamentally different financing basis was intended, and added a time-limit provision as advised.
concerns: The Afdeling finds the efficiency rationale for financing the SER via the Awf insufficiently motivated and advises a fuller justification, which the government expanded in the explanatory memorandum.
The Afdeling advises that a time-limited horizon clause be included as a pragmatic, temporary solution pending a fundamental reconsideration of financing, which the government adopted.

The Afdeling notes that financing from general revenue in case of an Awf deficit contradicts the stated continuity of employer-only financing and advises clarification, which the government addressed by clarifying the explanatory memorandum.

33490.s: The bill amends the Dutch Plant Protection and Biocides Act to implement EU Regulation 528/2012 on biocides, replacing the old directive-based rules with direct references to the regulation. It designates the Ctgb as competent authority, sets prohibitions and penalty links, and gives the Minister and Ctgb limited powers for temporary exemptions and restrictions.
33490.j: The memorandum justifies the exemption power by pointing to exceptional situations and possible consequences, and proposes retaining it with the Minister instead of transferring it to the competent authority.
q: Given the exceptional situations and the possible consequences of exemption decisions, it is proposed not to transfer this power to the authority that is normally competent.
Gezien de uitzonderlijke situaties en de mogelijke gevolgen van vrijstellingsbesluiten wordt voorgesteld om deze bevoegdheid niet over te dragen aan de, in het normale geval bevoegde autoriteit
d: exemptions for defence interests and labelling rules for biocides
fee payment and procedure for exemption applications
rules on fees for biocide authorisation
p: The Minister may grant exemptions from biocide prohibitions for up to 180 days for unavoidable health or environmental dangers, including immediate effect without normal publication.
The Ctgb is empowered to temporarily restrict or prohibit placing a biocide on the market where there are clear indications of serious risk.

parties: Asks whether national supplementary policy is still possible, whether the Ctgb is ready for its new workload, and how enforcement compares across member states.
The VVD members are concerned whether supervision and enforcement powers are properly arranged or will be in these countries.
De leden van de VVD-fractie zijn bezorgd of het toezicht en de handhavingsbevoegdheden wel goed geregeld zijn of worden in deze landen.
Asks what the simplified procedure for low-risk biocides means for Dutch national assessment and whether a national ban remains possible.
Does this mean, for example, that the Netherlands no longer assesses itself whether a plant protection product can be authorised?
Betekent dit bijvoorbeeld dat Nederland niet meer zelf beoordeelt of een gewasbeschermingsmiddel toegelaten kan worden?
Worries about a race to the bottom in EU authorisation, asks for checks and balances, independence of the Ctgb, and reversal of the burden of proof.
How does the government intend to prevent a race to the bottom in which all applications go to the country that interprets the rules most leniently or has a poor-quality college?
Hoe wil de regering voorkomen dat er een race naar de bodem ontstaat waarbij alle aanvragen gaan naar het land dat de regels het soepelst interpreteert of een kwalitatief slecht college heeft?
Asks on what urgent grounds the Netherlands may deviate from mutual recognition and why a fallback provision for missing assessment methods was not included.
Article 37 of Regulation 528/2012 allows member states a number of deviations from mutual recognition.
Artikel 37 van Verordening 528/2012 staat de lidstaten een aantal afwijkingen op wederzijdse erkenning toe.
Asks for clarification of 'urgent societal reasons' and 'demonstrable societal need' for hazardous biocides authorised under restrictive conditions.
The D66 members ask the government to explain what it understands by 'clear demonstrable societal need' for the use of biocides with a clear hazard risk.
De leden van de D66-fractie vragen de regering toe te lichten wat zij verstaan onder «duidelijke aantoonbare maatschappelijke noodzaak» voor het gebruik van biociden met een duidelijk gevarenrisico.
Questions the choice of a regulation over a directive because it removes member state policy freedom, and asks why fees apply to mutual recognition.
How does the government assess that, by choosing a regulation, member states no longer have policy freedom to decide for themselves how to meet the European biocide objectives, these members ask.

Hoe beoordeelt de regering dat er door de keuze voor een verordening geen beleidsvrijheid meer is voor lidstaten om zelf te bepalen hoe zij willen voldoen aan de Europese doelen op het gebied van biociden, zo vragen deze leden.
Supports harmonisation and simplified authorisation for less harmful biocides but asks about fees as a barrier for SMEs and the use of the Article 37 deviation option.
Is it the government's aim to use this deviation option as limitedly as possible?
Is het de inzet van de regering om deze afwijkingsmogelijkheid zo beperkt mogelijk te gebruiken?
Objects to reduced transparency of industry studies, asks for public disclosure as environmental information, and doubts independence of comparative evaluations.
Can the government confirm that, with the implementation of this regulation, even more data will be kept secret than has been the case until now?
Kan de regering bevestigen dat er nu, met de uitvoering van deze verordening, nog meer gegevens geheim gehouden worden dan tot nu toe het geval was?

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division supports the bill implementing EU Regulation 528/2012 on biocides but raises technical points: designating the competent authority for Article 27, criminalising breaches of Articles 17(6) and 27(1), clarifying the administrative fine, and applying the Act in the EEZ. The government's reply (nader rapport) reports that all points were followed, with amendments to the bill and memorandum.
concerns: The Council advised that the College voor de toelating be designated to carry out the competent-authority tasks under Article 27 of the Regulation, which was not regulated in the bill.
The Council advised criminalising breaches of Articles 17(6) and 27(1) of the Regulation, which the bill omitted from the criminal provision.

The Council noted that Article 46 imposes no obligation and that the proposed amendment of Article 90 did not achieve the intended administrative fine; the bill was adjusted via the criminal prohibition in Article 43(4).
The Council advised expressly declaring the Act's relevant provisions applicable in the Dutch exclusive economic zone for legal certainty, which was done with a new Article 41.
The Council made editorial remarks on cross-references and definitions, which were adopted.

33508.s: The bill amends the Dutch Medical Research Involving Human Subjects Act to allow research with minors and adults who cannot consent, permitting slightly more than minimal risk for non-beneficial research and adding requirements such as a pediatrician on review committees. It also moves and removes some protective provisions, such as the obligation to define and monitor risks and burden for drug research, and the opposition clause, into general rules.
33508.j: The memorandum justifies the changes by the need for accessible research and better care for children and incapacitated adults, and by the proportionality of the rights limitation.
q: Allowing scientific research on people who cannot themselves give consent may limit their private life or bodily integrity.

Het toelaten van wetenschappelijk onderzoek met mensen die daarvoor zelf geen toestemming kunnen geven, kan een beperking van de persoonlijke levenssfeer of de onaantastbaarheid van het lichaam inhouden.

parties: Asks why the government retained the absolute risk ceiling, how the CCMO and Raad van State advice was weighed, and how the review framework and DSMC role will work.
What led the government to decide to nevertheless retain the upper limit?
Wat heeft de regering ertoe doen besluiten de bovengrens alsnog te handhaven?
Supports the goal of enabling research but asks who will draft the review framework and whether ethics committees have the necessary expertise.
How can the government guarantee that the METC will ensure the necessary expertise when protocols for research on incapacitated adults are assessed by a METC?
Op welke wijze kan de regering waarborgen dat de METC zorg zal dragen voor de benodigde expertise wanneer protocollen voor onderzoek met wilsonbekwame meerderjarigen door een METC wordt beoordeeld?
Views the bill as departing too far from the March 2012 draft and finds the justification for the ceiling insufficient, asking for more room for intervention research.
Questions the balance between individual and group interests, the departure from Doek commission advice, and whether the bill complies with Article 7 ICCPR and the Oviedo Convention.
Have the proposals in this bill struck a correct balance between the interests of the individual and the group interest?
Is met de voorstellen in dit wetsvoorstel een juiste balans gevonden tussen de belangen van het individu en het groepsbelang?
Welcomes consultation but stresses extreme care for vulnerable groups, asks how patients are protected and who decides for incapacitated persons.
Does this amendment of the WMO provide sufficient safeguards to protect the patient?
Geeft deze wijziging van de WMO voldoende waarborgen om de patiënt te beschermen?
Asks for a chronological account of how the bill changed from the Doek advice and the earlier draft, and how case-specific factors are weighed.
These members would like to see a precise, chronological description of the developments surrounding this amendment.
Genoemde leden zouden graag een nauwkeurige, chronologische beschrijving zien van de ontwikkelingen rond deze wetswijziging.
Stresses child protection and proportionality of risks and benefits, and asks for a response to patient organisations who consider the bill a step back.
Given the vulnerability of especially young children, it is very important to place sufficient emphasis on protecting children in research.
Gezien de kwetsbaarheid van, vooral jonge, kinderen is het van groot belang om voldoende nadruk te leggen op bescherming van kinderen bij onderzoek.
Asks how the bill guarantees that research on children is only used when adults cannot be studied, how vague risk terms are bounded, and how parents and representatives are involved.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advises, in its opinion of 3 December 2014, that the second amendment note to the WMO bill (research with minors and incapacitated adults) must be revised: it extends the EU Regulation 536/2014 criterion to all non-therapeutic research without a substantive weighing against the protection of vulnerable subjects, and leaves unclear the treatment of adults lacking capacity, subjects without a condition, and the meaning of 'standaardbehandeling'. In the government's reply (nader rapport) of 10 March 2015, the minister explains the uniformity rationale, the bounded-risk approach, and that the CCMO/NVMETC testing framework and further safeguards will address the concerns, while the lowering of the age limit to sixteen was not objected to.
concerns: The extension of the relative EU criterion to all non-therapeutic research with minors and incapacitated adults needs a substantive weighing against protecting vulnerable subjects, not merely uniformity; the government adds clarification to the explanatory note but maintains uniformity.

The protection of vulnerable subjects under the stricter regime (nee, tenzij principle and absolute upper bound) must be weighed; the government maintains the statutory upper bound but says individual circumstances will determine the limit.

The meaning of 'standaardbehandeling' and its application to research without a condition or standard treatment must be clarified in the explanatory note; the government clarifies this and refers to the testing framework.
Treatment of adult incapacitated persons is not addressed in the explanatory note and requires reasoned justification for applying the EU criterion to them.

v.summary: The Council of State advisory division advised revising the bill amending the WMO to allow non-therapeutic research with minors and incapacitated adults, mainly by writing a clear upper risk bound into the statute, limiting such review to experienced METCs, and motivating compliance with Article 7 ICCPR. The government's reply states it adopted the advice on the upper bound and addressed the other points, including clarifying the international context and harmonising the position of minors and adults.
concerns: The Council advised writing a clear statutory upper bound on risk and burden for non-therapeutic research with minors and incapacitated adults, which the government adopted in article 3.

The Council doubted that all METCs have enough experience to assess research with incapacitated subjects and suggested limiting such review to experienced committees, with the government indicating it will examine concentration with the CCMO.
The Council advised motivating in the explanatory memorandum that the bill remains compatible with article 7 ICCPR safeguards even without the current criteria, which the government did in its reply.
The Council advised aligning the wording and explanation for minors and adult incapacitated persons and made several editorial remarks, which were largely taken into account.

33526.s: The bill extends several provisions of Book 1 and Book 10 of the Civil Code concerning parenthood, recognition, custody and guardianship to registered partnerships, placing them on par with marriage. It also allows dissolution of registered partnerships without a judge in certain cases, adds a registry-based guardianship designation, and sets transitional and co-ordination rules with a separate bill on parenthood.
33526.j: The explanatory memorandum justifies the changes by equal treatment of registered partnerships and marriage and by simplification, not by any expansion of executive power.
q: It is now considered justified, from the standpoint of equal treatment of married men and men who have entered a registered partnership, to remove this judicial review.

Het wordt thans verantwoord geacht om vanuit het oogpunt van gelijke behandeling van gehuwde mannen en mannen die een geregistreerd partnerschap zijn aangegaan, deze rechterlijke toets te laten vervallen.

parties: Asks whether partners entering a registered partnership understand the obligations, which resemble marriage, and whether children may be legally exploited for false recognitions.
Can grandchildren also request annulment of their grandparents' marriage?
Kunnen ook kleinkinderen de nietigverklaring van het huwelijk van hun grootouders verzoeken?
Asks how the advice of the Raad voor de rechtspraak and the Raad van State on cross-references in the guardianship and contact provisions has been weighed.
These members are curious how this advice is assessed, given that the Council of State's advisory division does recommend including that reference and that advice has been adopted.

Voornoemde leden zijn benieuwd hoe dit advies wordt beoordeeld, gelet op het feit dat de Afdeling advisering van de Raad van State wel adviseert de genoemde verwijzing op te nemen en dit advies is overgenomen.
Asks the government to respond to the KNB's criticism that testamentary guardianship no longer needs a notarial deed, removing a safeguard.
These members ask the government to respond to the KNB's comments on not making the arrangement of guardianship by notarial deed mandatory.
Deze leden vragen de regering te reageren op het commentaar door de KNB op het niet verplicht stellen van het regelen van de voogdij middels een notariële akte.
Asks what safeguards protect unfit parents and heirs when children may seek annulment and when guardianship is registered without a notary.
What safeguards are there for this, as the KNB also asks?
Welke waarborgen zijn hiervoor, zoals de KNB ook vraagt?
Asks whether dropping the judicial approval requirement for recognition is fully offset by the public-order provisions, and how conflicting guardianship declarations are resolved by the court.
Does this mean that in the new situation the same outcome will be reached in all cases as currently under article 204, first paragraph, part e?
Is hiermee bedoeld dat in de nieuwe situatie in alle voorkomende gevallen dezelfde uitkomst zal worden bereikt als thans op grond van onderdeel e van artikel 204, eerste lid?
Objects to removing judicial review of recognition of a child born outside the marriage, arguing it weakens safeguards and the lifelong character of marriage.
Does this not in fact provide a safeguard against too easy recognition of a child not born from one's own marriage?
Biedt dit niet juist een waarborg voor een al te gemakkelijke erkenning van een kind dat niet geboren is uit het eigen huwelijk?

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a bill amending the Civil Code and Code of Civil Procedure to remove remaining differences between registered partnership and marriage, raising concerns about the inconsistency between the contact-ban grounds for parents with custody (art. 1:253a BW) and the stricter grounds for visitation of non-custodial parents (art. 1:377a BW), and about the legal basis for a centrally held custody register. The government's nader rapport accepted the first point by referring to the art. 1:377a(3) grounds and explained the custody register remains with the courts, so no central-register legal basis is needed yet.
concerns: The Afdeling found it hard to understand why contact-ban grounds for a parent without custody are much stricter than for a parent with custody, and advised aligning them; the government now refers to the art. 1:377a(3) grounds in art. 1:253a(2)(a).

The Afdeling noted the explanatory memorandum and rechtspraak.nl are inconsistent on how the central custody register operates and advised clarifying the legal basis; the government clarified the explanatory memorandum and committed to amending the Besluit gezagsregisters.
The Afdeling gave several redactional comments, which the government said were taken into account.

33544.s: The bill amends the 2013 budget statements of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (V) and of Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation (XVII) through an incidental supplementary budget, shifting appropriations across policy articles and setting the amounts in thousands of euros. It takes effect on 2 January 2013, with retroactive effect if the Staatsblad is published later.
q: We Beatrix, by the grace of God, Queen of the Netherlands, Princess of Orange-Nassau, etc. etc. etc. To all who shall see or hear read these presents, greetings!
Wij Beatrix, bij de gratie Gods, Koningin der Nederlanden, Prinses van Oranje-Nassau, enz. enz. enz. Allen, die deze zullen zien of horen lezen, saluut!

33553.s: The bill merges the twelve regional Chambers of Commerce, the association Kamer van Koophandel Nederland and foundation Syntens into a single national Kamer van Koophandel with its own governance (a board, a Centrale Raad and regional councils), defining its tasks, financing and supervision. It also amends numerous related laws to replace references to the old chambers and transfers staff, assets and liabilities to the new body.
33553.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations by the need for national uniform frameworks and ministerial oversight of a reorganised body, and for transitional flexibility during the merger.
q: By general measure of administration there is the possibility to set further rules on the statutory tasks.
Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur bestaat de mogelijkheid nadere regels te stellen over de wettelijke taken.
d: minister may delegate mandate, power of attorney or authorization to the Kamer for digital entrepreneurs' platform acts
rules on establishing and abolishing regions and regional branches
rules on participation in entrepreneurs' platforms, including exclusion or minister's prior consent
further rules on the statutory tasks of the Kamer
rules implementing EU acts on issuing declarations
rules for Kamer work, including prohibiting certain activities
rules on budget format and equity requirements
maximum monthly spending before budget approval
exemption from prior-consent requirement below a set amount
introduction and rules for a registration fee
general measure of administration deviating from civil service pay rules for transferred staff
transitional rules on consequences of the transfer, valid until end of following year
p: The minister may withhold budget approval, earmark funds for specific tasks and reduce future contributions when spending deviates from the earmark.
Minister must approve extra tasks and certain investments and can attach conditions and restrictions to his consent.
Minister may appoint board members without a nomination if the Chamber misses a deadline and may deviate from nominations on motivated grounds, weakening the role of business and employee bodies.
Rules on Kamer-created entities and codes of conduct are placed under ministerial approval, which can be refused for conflict with law or public interest.

parties: Asks how a one-off registration fee will be kept limited and prevented from growing uncontrolled or being used for other activities, and how the criteria for private partner access will be judged.
How is it prevented that this fee rises uncontrolled and is used to cover all kinds of other activities?
Hoe wordt voorkomen dat die vergoeding ongecontroleerd oploopt en wordt gebruikt ter dekking van allerhande andere activiteiten?
Questions the scope of digital-first policy, regional spread, the registration fee, use of residual funds, and wants clearer criteria and monitoring of administrative burden goals.
How and by whom are the objectives monitored and evaluated?
Hoe en door wie worden de doelstellingen gemonitord en geëvalueerd?
Asks why the registration fee was not submitted for advice to the Raad van State and seeks criteria and information to parliament on introducing the fee.
Why was this option not submitted for advice to the Council of State?
Waarom is deze mogelijkheid niet voorgelegd voor advies aan de Raad van State?
Supports modernisation in principle but questions oversight of tasks, the absence of a supervisory board, and the Council of State's warning about confusion with the portal.
Why has the government not chosen that? These members regret this choice and are considering submitting an amendment on this point.
Waarom heeft de regering daar niet voor gekozen. Deze leden betreuren deze keuze en overwegen op dit punt een amendement in te dienen.
Finds the scope of tasks inconsistent with returning to core tasks, questions the new levy and ministerial oversight, and wants market-overlap tasks cut more sharply.
If a task is already carried out by the market, then the Chamber has no business in that area.
Als een taak reeds door de markt wordt uitgevoerd, dan heeft de Kamer op dat terrein niets te zoeken.
Supports the transition in principle but wants to prevent the registration fee being used to fill budget gaps or deter new entrepreneurs, and asks about the removal of the supervisory board.
These members want to prevent this registration fee being used to fill budget cut gaps.
Deze leden willen voorkomen dat deze inschrijfvergoeding gebruikt wordt om bezuinigingsgaten te dekken.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on the draft Chamber of Commerce Act, raising major objections on the scope of facultative tasks, overlap with Agentschap NL, the public-private character of entrepreneurs' squares, the removal of business representatives from the board, and the designation of the ministry to set up the digital portal. The government's nader rapport accepts most points, adding ministerial approval for new facultative tasks and a mandated multi-year programme, while keeping the core governance choice with justification.
concerns: The Afdeling asked for clearer definition and justification of the facultative tasks the Chamber may undertake, which the government addressed by requiring ministerial approval for new tasks.
The Afdeling found the relationship and task division with Agentschap NL unclear and overlapping; the government clarified responsibilities but largely maintained the structure.
The Afdeling questioned the inclusion of private service providers on public entrepreneurs' squares and the risk of confusion; the government added a basis for rules on participation.

The Afdeling considered the removal of employer and employee representatives from the Chamber's board insufficiently motivated and changing its character; the government added a central council with programming powers but kept the board structure.
The Afdeling asked that the ministry's role in setting up the digital entrepreneurs' square be convincingly justified; the government explained the link with existing duties.
The Afdeling asked that the minister approve the multi-year programme and that the status of the regional programme be clarified; the government made both changes.
The Afdeling asked that the explanatory memorandum state the amount of the financing shifted to the EL&I budget; the government added this information.
The Afdeling gave a number of redactional comments on definitions and wording, which the government largely adopted.

33580.s: The bill amends the Dutch Criminal Code to implement EU Directive 2011/93/EU on sexual abuse and exploitation of children, adding a new article 248f criminalising causing a minor under 18 to engage in sexual acts through coercion, and raising maximum prison sentences by one third for offences against vulnerable persons or involving violence. It also adjusts the Besluit justitiële en strafvorderlijke gegevens to implement the directive.
33580.j: The memorandum justifies the bill as implementation of an EU directive and says the directive's provisions can be given effect within the existing general legal framework, with discretion left to prosecutors and judges.
q: For that reason I propose adding the circumstance that abuse of a vulnerable position is made to the aggravating grounds in article 248 of the Criminal Code.
Om die reden stel ik voor om de omstandigheid dat misbruik van een kwetsbare positie wordt gemaakt aan de strafverzwaringsgronden zoals vervat in artikel 248 Sr toe te voegen.

parties: Asks how the legality principle fits with undefined 'seksuele gedraging' and whether the term should be statutorily defined.
