34219.j: The memorandum justifies the independence and delegation of rule-making to the authority by reference to EU and IAEA requirements for an independent regulator free of political influence, and the CJEU Commission v Germany ruling.
q: A strong regulatory body with genuine independence in its decision-making is considered a fundamental requirement of the Community regulatory framework for nuclear safety.

Een sterk regulerend lichaam met daadwerkelijke onafhankelijkheid in haar besluitvorming wordt een fundamenteel vereiste gevonden van het regelgevende kader van de Gemeenschap voor nucleaire veiligheid.
d: authority may set rules on organisational and technical matters of nuclear safety, radiation protection and security
p: The minister may not issue policy rules on how the authority carries out its tasks, removing a ministerial steering instrument over the authority's work.
The minister may annul authority decisions only for conflict with law, not on public-interest grounds, and must notify parliament of any annulment.
The minister appoints, suspends and dismisses board members and funds the authority, with the reasons for dismissal disclosed only on request.

parties: Asks whether the minister has sufficient instruments to ensure the ANVS performs its tasks responsibly and asks about the limits of general policy rules that could affect the ANVS's independence.
Does the government have sufficient instruments at hand to ensure that the ANVS carries out its tasks properly and responsibly, the VVD members ask.
Heeft de regering voldoende instrumenten in handen om te waarborgen dat de ANVS haar taken naar behoren en op verantwoordelijke wijze uitvoert, zo vragen de leden van de VVD-fractie.
Asks how independence is guaranteed in terms of finances, staff and expertise, and whether the minister should be able to annul ANVS decisions in the public interest.
The PvdA members ask why it was not chosen to give the minister the possibility to annul ANVS decisions on grounds of the public interest.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie vragen waarom er niet voor is gekozen de Minister de mogelijkheid te geven besluiten van de ANVS te vernietigen op grond van het algemeen belang.
Asks how the ANVS is kept from becoming detached, questions the lack of a clear account of oversight of the ANVS, and asks about the reporting to parliament.
They miss in the bill a clear explanation of the oversight of the ANVS.
Zij missen in het wetsvoorstel een heldere uiteenzetting van het toezicht op de ANVS.

Asks for earlier parliamentary reporting on the ANVS, questions the lack of a provision guaranteeing information access from government, and raises concerns about the minister's annulment power and staff appointment powers.
These members ask whether the government would be willing to share the first experiences with the functioning of this ANVS with parliament sooner than after five years.
Deze leden vragen of de regering bereid zou zijn om op kortere termijn dan na vijf jaar de eerste ervaringen met het functioneren van deze ANVS te delen met het parlement.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on a bill establishing the Autoriteit Nucleaire Veiligheid en Stralingsbescherming, questioning the complete exclusion of ministerial policy rules and the limitation of annulment to unlawfulness, and asking for clarification on capacity, external support, information exchange and transposition. The government's nader rapport accepts most points, amending the memorie van toelichting on policy rules and annulment, adding statutory bases for external expertise and information exchange, and completing the implementation table, while leaving some transposition to a later stage.
concerns: The Afdeling found the total exclusion of ministerial policy rules insufficiently justified, since framework-setting general policy rules are compatible with the independence requirement; the government amended the explanatory memorandum but did not change the exclusion.

The Afdeling found no compelling reasons shown for restricting the ministerial annulment power to unlawfulness instead of the general grounds of article 10:35 Awb; the government adjusted the explanatory memorandum and clarified which decisions are covered.
The Afdeling asked how the bill addresses the capacity shortage identified in the Berenschot report on radiation protection; the government supplemented the explanatory note on article 3(h).
The Afdeling asked for explicit provision allowing the regulator to call on external scientific and technical expertise as required by Directive 2014/87; the government amended article 3(3)(i).
The Afdeling found no statutory basis for exchanging information from supervisory activities with foreign regulators; the government added a new provision (article 3(3)(f)).

The Afdeling noted that the implementation table omitted other articles of the directive relevant to the regulator; the government supplemented the explanation and stated a complete table will follow later.

34228.s: The bill allows landlords and tenants of residential property to agree an energy performance fee, paid by the tenant for a landlord-guaranteed energy performance from energy-saving and energy-generating installations, by adding a new Civil Code article 7:261a and a new section 19a to the Rent Price Implementation Act. The Rent Commission would review the reasonableness of such fees, with the conditions and maximum amount to be set by general administrative order (AMvB).
34228.j: The memorandum justifies the AMvB route by flexibility, so that amounts and conditions can respond to new developments such as innovative applications, and it states that a maximum amount protects the tenant.
q: For reasons of flexibility, it has been chosen to set the maximum amounts by general administrative order.
Uit oogpunt van flexibiliteit is ervoor gekozen om de maximumbedragen bij algemene maatregel van bestuur vast te stellen.
d: Artikel II C (artikel 19a lid 2 Uitvoeringswet huurprijzen woonruimte)
maximum amount of energy performance fee
Artikel II C (artikel 19a lid 3 Uitvoeringswet huurprijzen woonruimte)
cases and conditions for agreeing energy performance fee
p: Artikel II C (artikel 19a lid 2 en 3 Uitvoeringswet huurprijzen woonruimte)
Key ceilings and eligibility conditions for the energy performance fee are left to an AMvB without parliamentary approval, though the Rent Commission retains review of reasonableness.

parties: Asks whether a marginal review rather than an open 'reasonableness' standard for the Huurcommissie would be more appropriate, and questions the discretion left to lower regulation.
These members ask the government whether a marginal review would not have been more appropriate.
Deze leden vragen de regering of een marginale toetsing niet meer voor de hand had gelegen
Wants firm protection of tenants' total housing costs, a proof of the General Measure of Administration before plenary debate, and clarity on whether tenants can refuse the fee.
These members also attach importance to good protection of individual tenants and demand that the law firmly safeguard total housing costs.
Deze leden hechten ook aan een goede bescherming van de individuele huurders en verlangen in de wet een goede borging van de totale woonlasten.
Asks how tenants can object to the fee, what remedies exist, and how the amount and energy measurements are determined and checked against fraud.
The question also arises where tenants can turn if they disagree with the determination of heat demand and generating capacity or with the amount of the fee.
Tevens luidt de vraag waar huurders heen kunnen wanneer zij het niet eens zijn met het bepalen van de warmtevraag en de opwekcapaciteit of met de hoogte van de vergoeding.
Asks why the maximum fee is tied to a fixed factor and requests a per-municipality overview of affordable housing, information the Chamber needs to scrutinise the bill.
These members ask whether the government can provide an overview per municipality of the amount of affordable housing for the target group.
Daarom vragen deze leden of de regering een overzicht kan geven per gemeente van de omvang van betaalbare woningen voor de doelgroep.
Raises questions on double charging with the Warmtewet and tax, and notes the absence of an evaluation clause in the bill.
The D66 members note that an evaluation provision is missing from the bill.
De leden van de D66-fractie constateren dat een evaluatiebepaling in het voorliggende wetsvoorstel ontbreekt.

Supports the bill's climate aims but asks for the maximum-fee general measure to be submitted to the Chamber, for standard contracts and evaluation, and for tenants' remedies against underperforming installations.
These members suggest submitting this general measure of administration to the Chamber so it can review the elaboration of the proposal.
Deze leden geven in overweging deze algemeen maatregel van bestuur wel voor te hangen zodat de Kamer de uitwerking van het voorstel kan toetsen
Worries about whether tenants are adequately protected against excessive increases and proposes annual monitoring and evaluation with possible amendment of the general measure.
Member Van Vliet is concerned about the tenant's position. Is the tenant adequately protected against an excessive increase?
Het lid Van Vliet maakt zich zorgen om de positie van de huurder. Wordt de huurder wel afdoende beschermd tegen een te hoge verhoging?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised that the bill allowing landlord and tenant to agree an energy performance fee should be better justified or, if the fee falls outside the rent, be placed in the Civil Code alongside the utility-cost rule of article 7:237 BW. The government's reply states the advice was largely followed: the fee is now in article 7:237 BW and a new article 19a of the Uitvoeringswet huurprijzen woonruimte, with clarifications in the explanatory memorandum.
concerns: The Afdeling said the explanation for why the energy performance fee falls outside the rent was insufficient and that the provision should sit in the Civil Code system, which the government adopted.
The Afdeling proposed simplifying the wording of the proposed article 18a, which was partly adopted in the reworded provision.
The Afdeling asked that passages giving concrete content to a yet-to-be-adopted AMvB be removed; the government reviewed and partly reformulated or deleted them.

34264.s: The bill modernises the Dutch public media system by sharpening the public media mandate, expanding the NPO's steering and coordinating powers, and allowing external proposals to be aired on public channels. It also creates a new governance structure for the regional public broadcaster (RPO) with its own board, supervisory board and concession plan, and abolishes the Mediafonds and fixed broadcasting-time guarantees.
34264.j: The memorandum justifies the expanded NPO powers as necessary for daadkracht, efficiency and modernisation of the broadcasting system, while stressing that editorial independence and government non-interference are preserved.
d: Artikel I, onder K (art. 2.172, derde lid)
rules on content and layout of the annual accounts, including cost of programming
rules on structure and submission timing of the RPO concession policy plan
further rules on content and layout of the RPO budget
p: Artikel I, onder P (art. 2.53) and Q (art. 2.54)

The NPO board may take the initiative to have programmes made on proposals from outside parties and may direct the NTR to broadcast them, while removing previous fixed broadcasting-time guarantees for broadcasters.
The NPO supervisory board's supervisory scope is broadened and it is given a duty of information from the board, strengthening its position as an internal check.
Artikel I, onder S and U-V (art. 2.56, RPO provisions)
A single national RPO board and concession plan replace separate regional broadcaster governance, with the Minister's approval required for board appointments and parts of the concession plan.

parties: Asks how the bill prevents unfair competition with commercial music stations and about bandwidth for the NPO's fifth radio channel, without taking a firm position on checks.
How does this bill prevent unfair competition with commercial music stations arising from the broad Pop and Rock programming?
Hoe wordt met dit het wetsvoorstel voorkomen dat door de brede programmering van Pop en Rock oneerlijke concurrentie met commerciële muziekstations ontstaat?
Supports sharpening the public broadcaster's course and organisation, and welcomes clarity that entertainment remains part of the mission.
The members endorse the need to sharpen the course, mandate and manner of cooperation and organisation at the broadcasters.
De leden onderschrijven de noodzaak tot het verscherpen van de koers, de opdracht en de wijze van samenwerking en organiseren bij de omroepen.
Worries that the NPO takes over content decisions and steering from member broadcasters, and asks how independence and pluriformity are guaranteed.
Can the government clearly explain on what basis it expects the pluriformity and independence of the public broadcaster to remain assured, the members ask.
Kan de regering helder uiteenzetten waarop de verwachting is gebaseerd dat de pluriformiteit en onafhankelijkheid van de publieke omroep verzekerd zullen blijven, zo vragen de leden.

Notes the Raad van State recommended stricter criteria because the NPO's stronger role removes self-restraint, and the government did not adopt this; asks what keeps member broadcasters responsible for content.

May the members infer from the fact that the recommendation was not adopted that for the government self-restraint by the broadcasting associations remains the guiding principle to prevent improper competition with commercial media?

Mogen de leden uit het feit dat de aanbeveling niet overgenomen wordt, aflezen dat voor de regering (zelf)beperking vanuit de omroepverenigingen leidend blijft om te voorkomen dat er op oneigenlijke wijze geconcurreerd wordt met commerciële media?
Highlights inconsistency in removing entertainment while broadly permitting it as a means, and asks how programme quality and experimentation criteria will be set and supervised.
The government considers that the current mandate for public media institutions gives 'insufficient direction'.
De regering is namelijk van mening dat de huidige opdracht aan de publieke media-instellingen «onvoldoende richting» geeft.
Questions the tight timetable, the definition of amusement, whether innovation will be bureaucratised, and whether opening the system to externals guarantees pluriformity.
Does the government agree with these members that opening the system to externals offers no guarantee that pluriformity will be preserved?
Is de regering het met deze leden eens dat het openen van het bestel voor externen geen garantie biedt dat pluriformiteit gewaarborgd blijft?

Opposes centralised steering by a small body disconnected from society, questions the evidence for it, and fears loss of member-based democratic legitimacy and removal of broadcasting-time guarantees.
Also in view of experiences in other social sectors, they do not have the impression that this is the road to success.
Zij hebben, mede gezien de ervaringen in andere maatschappelijke sectoren, niet de indruk dat dit de weg naar succes is.
Asks what evidence shows the system is not future-proof, objects to state involvement in programme content, and questions democratic legitimacy of NPO programme assessment.
What democratic legitimacy is there for the NPO itself to assess programme proposals and then have them produced?
Welke democratische legitimatie is er om de NPO zelf programmavoorstellen te beoordelen en vervolgens te laten verzorgen?

v.summary: The Council of State advisory division advised against sending the bill to parliament until its remarks were addressed, arguing the NPO's shift to a regie role needs further statutory safeguards on pluralism, independence, the role of broadcast associations, EU state-aid and rights. The government's reply accepts some points (publieksbetrokkenheid, appointment procedure for the supervisory board, a quality guarantee on budget and airtime) but rejects removing airtime guarantees and detailed statutory rules on genre coordinators.
concerns: Independence of public media and prohibition of prior content control under Article 7 Constitution and Article 10 ECHR require stronger NPO independence and clearer rules for genre coordinators.
State appointment of the NPO supervisory board strengthens government grip on public broadcasting; independence should be increased, e.g. via a different appointment procedure.
The necessity of the reform before the 2016 mergers take effect is insufficiently motivated and the end perspective of a hybrid system is unclear.
The position of broadcast associations and the removal of airtime guarantees create uncertainty; their role should be clarified in the law.
Changes to the financing and role of broadcast associations and external producers raise EU state-aid (DAEB) and transparency questions.
Scope of the public media mission was too broad; the government did not adopt the advice to revise its formulation, and rights coordination text needed clarification.
Legal protection against NPO decisions, supervision overlap with the Commissariaat, and incompatibility rules were raised and largely addressed in the reply.

34273.s: This omnibus bill amends many social security and labour statutes under the Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment, including child benefit, widows' and orphans' benefits, pensions, dismissal law, the Participatiewet, unemployment benefits and disability schemes, tightening eligibility rules (e.g. the kostendelersnorm and the vangnet framework) and shifting detailed rules to general administrative orders and ministerial regulations. It also ends the Inspectie SZW's organisation-focused oversight of the UWV and SVB, leaving only effectiveness supervision and on-request investigations.
34273.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations mainly on the ground that the detailed rules are technical and need to be adjusted quickly, and justifies ending organisation-focused oversight by pointing to improved internal controls and single-audit arrangements.
q: Ending organisation-focused oversight does not prevent the Minister from instructing the Inspectorate to investigate aspects of internal management.
Het beëindigen van het organisatiegerichte toezicht laat verder onverlet dat de Minister de Inspectie opdracht kan verlenen tot het instellen van onderzoek naar aspecten van interne bedrijfsvoering.
d: ARTIKEL I, A (Algemene Kinderbijslagwet art. 7 zesde lid b, sub 5°)
schools designated for distance-based double child benefit
ARTIKEL VI, D (Burgerlijk Wetboek 7:671a, lid 11 / 7:669 terms)
conditions for dismissal permission (UWV or commission)
conditions for disregarding months before 1 May 2013 in contract duration
designating municipality for benefit where no registered address
conditions, terms and substantive elaboration of the vangnetuitkering
ARTIKEL VIII, Aa (Participatiewet art. 78#, transitional rule)
temporary application of previous norms for six months
ARTIKEL XIII, A (Wet arbeid en zorg art. 3:1a)
UWV may deviate from timing rule for pay reimbursement in special cases
ARTIKEL XVII, G (Wet financiering sociale verzekeringen art. 49 lid 3)
model for guarantee declaration under the regulation of eigenrisicodrager
information duties of UWV and SVB towards the Inspectie SZW
p: ARTIKEL XXVIII, D-N (Wet SUWI hoofdstuk 7, Inspectie SZW)

Ends the Inspectorate's organisation-focused oversight of the UWV and SVB and its audit of their lawfulness, leaving the minister to rely on the organisations' own accountability and on-request investigations.
The Minister may reduce, withdraw or refuse safety-net payments to municipalities where the municipality breaches a legal rule, with the review committee advising on requests.</description_en>
Dismissal permission is refused where a dismissal prohibition applies, unless the prohibition is expected to lapse within four weeks, narrowing protection for workers only partly.</description_en>
Allows an amvb to designate a different municipality responsible for benefit payments to people without a registered address.

parties: Asks for a schematic overview of technical and policy changes and questions whether abolishing organisation-level oversight of the SVB is wise given ICT problems.
The VVD members request, partly following an earlier adopted motion, that the Chamber be sent a schematic overview of the technical and policy changes (even if they are small).

De leden van de VVD-fractie verzoeken (mede naar aanleiding eerder aangenomen motie) om de Kamer een schematisch overzicht van de technische wijzigingen en beleidswijzigingen te doen toekomen (ook al zijn deze klein).
Asks about the consequences of dropping the concentration of Wav-fine appeals at the Hague court and how the Moroccan social security treaty relates to the bill.

Following the Council of State's advice, the PvdA, SP, CDA and D66 members note that the concentration of appeals against Wav fines at the Hague district court was dropped on that advice, but was part of the 2016–2018 cost-cutting operation, and ask what the consequences are for that operation.

Naar aanleiding van het advies van de Raad van State vragen de leden van PvdA-, SP-, CDA-, D66 fracties, constaterende dat de concentratie van het beroep tegen Wav-boetes bij de rechtbank Den Haag op advies van de Raad van State is vervallen, maar dat dit wel onderdeel uitmaakte van de Taakstellingsoperatie 2016–2018, wat de gevolgen zijn voor deze operatie nu de beoogde concentratie niet doorgaat.
Questions the effects on municipalities and the adequacy of the budget and the safety-net rules, and asks how both chambers will be involved in the AMvB.
In what way will both Chambers be involved in the drafting of the AMvB?
Op welke wijze worden beide Kamers betrokken bij de totstandkoming van de AMvB?
Asks why municipalities are not given discretion to waive claims for information-duty breaches and about the treatment of partners in the kostendelersnorm.
Asks whether retroactive effect could force people to repay benefits already paid and whether the Remigratiewet change should go through a separate bill.
They ask why parts of the bill have retroactive effect.
Zij vragen waarom er voor onderdelen van het wetsvoorstel sprake is van terugwerkende kracht.
Asks about consequences for workers of retroactive obligations under WW article 20 and about the financial impact of dropping the Wav-fine concentration.
They ask for an explanation of the consequences for employees if new obligations apply to them with retroactive effect.
Zij vragen om een toelichting op de consequenties die voor werknemers kunnen optreden als met terugwerkende kracht nieuwe verplichtingen van toepassing op de werknemer worden.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised against the proposed concentration of Wav fine appeals at the Rechtbank Den Haag, flagged that the Anw woonlandbeginsel cannot apply to several countries under bilateral treaties and that retroactive effect conflicts with legal certainty, and found the required renunciation of Dutch nationality for remigration benefits insufficiently motivated. The government reply accepted the advice to drop the concentration and retroactivity provisions, removed the Remigratiewet and Faillissementswet changes from the bill, and made several technical amendments.
concerns: Retroactive effect of the Anw amendment conflicts with legal certainty and was dropped, with effect from 1 January 2017.
Justification for concentrating Wav fine appeals at the Rechtbank Den Haag is insufficient; the provision was removed from the bill.
Bilateral social security treaties preclude applying the woonlandbeginsel in the Anw for several countries; the explanatory memorandum was supplemented.
Requiring renunciation of Dutch nationality for remigration benefits lacks a sufficient justification; the change was removed from the bill.
Omnibus bill format is unsuitable for the politically sensitive court-concentration and nationality provisions; these were removed.
Technical corrections to articles and explanatory memorandum were made, including the Faillissementswet articles and redactional remarks.

34309.s: This bill replaces the detention regime for immigration detention (vreemdelingenbewaring) with a dedicated statutory framework, separating it from the penitentiary law, and sets out a non-punitive regime with differentiated accommodation, daily activities, contact rights and oversight bodies. It also grants the facility director wide order-and-security powers (force, searches, isolation, mechanical restraint, disciplinary measures) and extends detention periods and the reach of return-related obligations.
34309.j: The memorandum justifies the wide order-and-security powers by the need to protect staff, other detainees and the detainee in the event of serious incidents, and by the requirements of European and human-rights standards for a statutory basis.
q: This means that within the regime management and security measures must be applicable to maintain order and security in the facility.
Dit betekent dat binnen het regime beheers- en veiligheidsmaatregelen toegepast moeten kunnen worden ter handhaving van de orde en veiligheid in de inrichting.
d: Artikel 1, lid 2 / Artikel 21 / Artikel 36 (algemene maatregel van bestuur references)
detailed regime rules: room requirements, daily activity hours, detention criteria
criteria for placement in the management regime
criteria and procedure for placement and transfer of detainees
criteria for placement in penitentiary-type facilities
house rules set by facility director under ministerial model
supervision rules, transport arrangements, designation of visiting organisations
powers, composition and working of supervisory committees
rules for processing personal data including biometric and body scans
Artikel 52, lid 4 / Artikel 54, lid 2 / Artikel 64, lid 4
rules on mechanical restraint, medical interventions and cell regime
p: The facility director is given broad powers to give orders, use force, impose isolation and disciplinary measures, with several decisions reserved to the director personally.}
Use of force and restraint, and disciplinary sanctions including fines and confinement, may be applied to detainees, subject to necessity and written reporting.
Exclusion from activities, solitary confinement and mechanical restraint can be ordered by the director for extended periods with renewal and complaint routes.
Searches of clothing, body scanning, manual body searches and removal of objects from body cavities are authorised with privacy safeguards.
Director may place detainees in the stricter management regime for up to six weeks, renewable, subject to a hearing and complaint route.
Director may collect and process personal data of detainees and visitors for identity and return purposes, including telecom numbers.
Force may be used to compel detainees to attend return-related activities and transport, extending coercive powers beyond order maintenance.
Supervisory committees retain access, complaint-handling and advisory roles over the facility.

parties: Asks what problem the bill solves, why voluntary rather than forced departure is emphasised, and how repeated detention affects return rates.
Should it not be stated first that the aliens covered by this bill have a duty to depart, and that detention follows from their failure to meet that duty?

Zou niet voorop gesteld moeten worden dat de vreemdelingen op wie dit wetsvoorstel betrekking heeft een vertrekplicht hebben en dat vreemdelingenbewaring een gevolg is van het feit dat zij niet voldoen aan deze vertrekplicht
Welcomes the humane, ultima ratio approach but asks whether the bill gives enough guarantees that alternatives are used more often and detention is reduced.
In general these members ask whether the law provides sufficient guarantees that alternatives will really be used more often and people placed in detention less often.
In het algemeen vragen deze leden of de wet voldoende garanties biedt zodat alternatieven echt vaker ingezet gaan worden en mensen minder vaak in detentie geplaatst worden.
Argues the bill falls short on ultima ratio and minimal restrictions, wants a duty to justify detention for all detainees, and opposes isolation cells, child detention and repeated detention.
It is a missed opportunity that the isolation cell, the practice of children in cells and the possibility of repeated detention remain in this bill.
Het is een gemiste kans dat de isoleercel, de praktijk van kinderen in de cel en de mogelijkheid tot herhaalde detentie in dit wetsvoorstel behouden zijn.
Asks for statistical substantiation of voluntary departure and effects on return rates, and whether the bill indirectly changes residence rules via lower-level regulation.
These members ask whether the government can substantiate with figures its conclusion that most aliens depart independently.
Deze leden vragen of de regering haar conclusie dat de meeste vreemdelingen zelfstandig vertrekken cijfermatig kan onderbouwen.
Wants a clear burden of proof on government in Article 58, judicial authorisation for children's coercive measures, a ban on children in cells, and a prior-consultation procedure for regulations.
These members ask the government to adopt lessons from other public institutions such as closed youth care, including judicial authorisation for coercive measures.
Voornoemde leden vragen de regering om lessen uit andere overheidsinstellingen zoals de gesloten jeugdzorg over te nemen.

Says the bill does not sufficiently meet the call for fundamental reform, questions repressive elements and penitentiary placement, and asks how detainees' rights are safeguarded without independent review of the regime.
The members ask the government to clearly justify why this very vulnerable group is not, in principle or as far as possible, not placed in detention.
De genoemde leden vragen de regering helder te onderbouwen waarom er niet voor is gekozen deze zeer kwetsbare groep vreemdelingen in beginsel niet, of zo min mogelijk, in bewaring te stellen.
Asks why the bill focuses only on detention rather than return obligations and why a separate Vreemdelingenwet structure was not chosen.
These members ask why return and the obligations resting on the alien in that respect are not given separate attention.
Deze leden vragen waarom niet afzonderlijk aandacht wordt gegeven aan terugkeer en de verplichtingen die dienaangaande op de vreemdeling rusten.
Asks for definitions of the two regimes and the conditions under which directors may place detainees in the restrictive regime, and about consequences for directors.
The members of Groep Kuzu/Öztürk would like to know whether the two types of regimes, the residence regime and the management regime, can be defined.
Graag vernemen de leden van de Groep Kuzu/Öztürk of de twee soorten regimes, het verblijfsregime en het beheersregime, kunnen worden gedefinieerd.
Asks about transitional law for proceedings begun before entry into force and how pending disputes will be handled under old versus new procedural rules.
They ask what happens to situations that began before the act took effect but continued after its entry into force.
Zij vragen wat er gebeurt met situaties die aanvingen voor de inwerkingtreding van de wet, maar wel doorliepen tot na de inwerkingtreding.
Asks why the bill emphasises alternatives to detention and what effect it will have on return figures.
Asks how transitional rules affect vulnerability of foreigners caught between regimes and how old and new material and procedural law will be applied in disputes.

Does this also mean that foreigners sometimes cannot invoke the rules in the bill that favour them, and conversely can be punished or reprimanded under rules that no longer apply after the bill takes effect?

Betekent dit ook dat vreemdelingen soms geen beroep kunnen doen op de voor hen gunstige regels uit het wetsvoorstel en vice versa gestraft of berispt kunnen worden op basis van regels die na invoering van het wetsvoorstel niet meer gelden?

Presses for criteria and central registration for decisions to detain instead of voluntary departure, for justification that lighter measures do not suffice, for limits on repeated detention beyond 18 months, and for a parliamentary pre-consultation procedure on the general administrative order.
These members ask whether there are criteria on the basis of which this assessment is made, or whether it is a wholly discretionary assessment.
Deze leden vragen of er criteria zijn op basis waarvan deze beoordeling wordt gemaakt, of dat het hier een volledig discretionaire beoordeling betreft.

Objects that the bill starts from 'yes, unless' rather than detention as ultimum remedium, says too many rules are left to a general administrative order, and wants them placed in the law or subjected to pre-consultation; also objects to visitation of body cavities and the strict management regime.
These members want those elements to be included in the law itself, or submitted to a pre-consultation procedure.
Deze leden willen dat die elementen alsnog in de wet zelf opgenomen worden, of in een voorhangprocedure worden voorgelegd.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division advised on the draft Wet terugkeer en vreemdelingenbewaring, raising major concerns that the detention regime is still penitentiary in character and not sufficiently justified by the principle of minimal restrictions, and that the ultimum remedium principle and the possibility of housing detention in penitentiary complexes need better justification. The government's nader rapport largely accepted the advice, adapting the bill on several points while rejecting or only partly following others, such as the delegation objections and the proposed change in name.
concerns: The detention regimes (beheersregime, blokuren, visiting hours) are insufficiently justified as necessary and as consistent with the principle of minimal restrictions, so the bill should be reconsidered.

Housing immigration detention in a complex that is also a penitentiary institution is insufficiently justified under the Return Directive, and detention of unaccompanied minors in prisons conflicts with the reception directive.
The ultimum remedium principle is formulated as 'ja, tenzij' instead of 'nee, tenzij' and should be aligned with the revised Procedure and Reception Directives.
Key regime-determining elements such as the criteria for detention and daily hours are delegated to lower regulation rather than set in the statute itself.
The judicial review standard for detention decisions must be aligned with the CJEU Mahdi judgment requiring intensive review.
Several technical and redactional points on the bill's wording and structure should be corrected.
The bill's name should reflect that it mainly concerns immigration detention rather than return.

34336.s: The bill amends the WIA-related laws to narrow the employer's own-risk liability for WGA benefits to claims whose waiting period starts on or after the date an employer becomes an own-risk bearer, and to create a tail-risk fund (staartlastenvermogen) financed from the Werkhervattingskas for pre-existing tail risks. It also updates cross-references and sets the effective date by royal decree.
34336.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations as necessary to implement the technical details of the own-risk and tail-risk arrangements through the Besluit Wfsv and ministerial rules.
q: The Besluit Wfsv will also be based on article 133#, second paragraph.
Het Besluit Wfsv zal mede worden gebaseerd op artikel 133#, tweede lid.
d: ARTIKEL I, B (art. 82, tweede lid; art. 83, eerste lid)
period of own-risk bearing for WGA benefits
partial limitation of transitional own-risk liability for categories of employers
rules on type and scope of costs recoverable from employers or insurers
ARTIKEL II, J (art. 117b, derde lid, onderdeel h)
part of WGA tail-risk benefits borne by the Werkhervattingskas
entry into force by royal decree, possibly differing per article
p: Own-risk liability is redefined and its duration and cost rules are left to ministerial regulation, widening executive discretion over employer obligations and recovery.
ARTIKEL II, C and J (tail-risk fund)
Financing of a tail-risk fund from the Werkhervattingskas is partly determined by general administrative order, shifting detailed funding decisions to the executive.

parties: Asks whether re-integration responsibility should stay with the guaranteeing insurer after bankruptcy and why a fund was not chosen.
Do you agree with these members that the level playing field is served when responsibility and costs lie in one hand?
Bent u het met deze leden eens dat het gelijk speelveld gediend is bij een situatie waarin verantwoordelijkheid en lasten in één hand liggen?
Asks how a shift to public insurance will be financed from the Werkhervattingskas and whether EMU-balance effects were calculated.
Can it therefore be explained to what extent this shift from private to public can in future be paid from the Werkhervattingskas?
Kan derhalve worden toegelicht in hoeverre deze verschuiving van privaat naar publiek in de toekomst betaald kan worden uit de Werkhervattingskas?
Doubts effectiveness of the bill; asks why a fully public system was not chosen and why no measures followed the Astri research.
The SP members have reservations about the effectiveness of the present bill and have several clarifying questions.
De leden van de SP-fractie hebben bedenkingen bij de effectiviteit van het voorliggende wetsvoorstel en hebben nog een aantal verduidelijkende vragen.
Supports the bill's goal of stronger incentives for prevention and reintegration; asks about reintegration after employer bankruptcy and UWV/Belastingdienst objections on switching moments.
They endorse the bill's aim to give employers and insurers more incentive to deploy prevention and reintegration optimally.
Zij onderschrijven het doel van het wetsvoorstel om de werkgevers en verzekeraars meer te prikkelen tot optimale inzet op preventie en re-integratie.
Expects a more level playing field; asks for quantified effects on premiums, the original purpose of the interest-windfall reserve, and whether the three-year switching period could trap employers.
They expect this bill to create a more level playing field between public and private implementation of the WGA.
Zij verwachten dat er met dit wetsvoorstel een gelijker speelveld ontstaat tussen de publieke en private uitvoering van de WGA.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division advised that the Wia/WGA hybrid-market bill may proceed, but asked for a substantive justification of the benefit of the hybrid system for prevention and reintegration and for adjustment of the financing of public tail costs (use of the rentehobbel reserve and a surcharge only on later switchers). The government's nader rapport largely rejects the objections on prevention, explains the use of the reserve and the surcharge, and adds clarifications and redactional changes.
concerns: The Afdeling asked for a substantive justification of the hybrid system's added value for prevention and reintegration, since the CPB found private firms do not perform better; the government acknowledges the point but argues new products and recent measures will improve the market and promises monitoring.

The Afdeling asked the government to explain why the rentehobbel reserve, originally meant for a level playing field, may now finance public tail costs; the government explained that employers who paid the surcharge already contributed, and clarified the text.

The Afdeling objected that the surcharge creates unequal premiums depending on the date of entry into the public scheme, leaving some employers and starters outside both the surcharge and the reserve; the government rejected retroactive correction as unfeasible and undesirable and kept the rule.
The Afdeling advised incorporating the measures announced in the government letter of 21 September 2015 and made redactional and technical remarks, which the government followed.

34345.s: The bill raises the statutory maximum prison sentences for human smuggling under Article 197a of the Dutch Criminal Code, from four to six years for the basic offence and up to eighteen years for aggravated forms. It implements EU framework decision obligations to deter facilitation of illegal entry with effective, proportionate and dissuasive sanctions.
34345.j: The memorandum justifies the higher maxima by EU framework decision obligations and the need for dissuasive sanctions and proportionate punishment of serious offences.
q: Under Framework Decision 2002/946/JHA on strengthening the penal framework to prevent facilitation of unauthorised entry, transit and residence, EU Member States are obliged to threaten human smuggling with effective, proportionate and dissuasive criminal sanctions.

Op grond van het Kaderbesluit 2002/946/JHA tot versterking van het strafrechtelijk kader voor de bestrijding van hulpverlening bij illegale binnenkomst, illegale doortocht en illegaal verblijf zijn de EU-lidstaten verplicht om mensensmokkel te bedreigen met effectieve, evenredige en afschrikwekkende strafrechtelijke sancties.

parties: Supports higher maxima given the gravity of smuggling, asks whether other EU states have seen a deterrent effect and whether smugglers can be prosecuted in their home countries.
Given the seriousness and consequences of these practices, an increase in the penalty range can fit well with that.
Gezien de ernst en gevolgen van deze praktijken kan een verhoging van de strafmaat daar goed bij passen.
Supports the increase as reflecting changed views on the seriousness of smuggling, stresses a holistic chain approach, and asks what data show a deterrent effect.
For this reason, these members support this amendment to the Criminal Code.
Daarom ondersteunen deze leden deze wijziging in het Wetboek van Strafrecht.
Agrees smugglers should be fought hard but questions whether a higher penalty deters non-Dutch smugglers unfamiliar with Dutch law and asks how the specific maxima were derived.
These members would like to hear the government's view on this.
Graag vernemen deze leden de visie van de regering hierop.
Supports higher penalties but asks about the effectiveness of the measures, the Ministerial Commission's recommendations, and the Raad van State's unanswered questions on effectiveness.
The members asked the government about the results achieved so far by the temporary Ministerial Commission on Migration.
De aan het woord zijnde leden vragen de regering naar de resultaten die de tijdelijke Ministeriële Commissie Migratie tot nu toe heeft geboekt.
Asks for data on perpetrators, prosecutions, convictions and actual sentences, and why rechters would impose heavier sentences given recent trafficking sentencing trends.
Why is it expected that judges will impose heavier sentences with an increase in the maximum penalty, now that it recently turned out that exactly the opposite happened in human trafficking?
Waarom wordt verwacht dat rechters zwaardere straffen zullen opleggen met een verhoging van het strafmaximum nu onlangs is gebleken dat bij mensenhandel precies het tegenovergestelde is gebeurd?

Questions the evidential basis and urgency, notes the Raad van State's advice for comparative research was ignored, and asks for consultation of the judiciary, bar and national rapporteur and for reconsideration of the entry-into-force date under the Consultative Referendum Act.

Is the government willing to conduct a comparative study after all into the extent to which migrant smuggling occurs in countries where maximum penalties are currently higher or lower than in the Netherlands?
Is de regering bereid alsnog een vergelijkend onderzoek te doen naar de mate waarin mensensmokkel plaatsvindt in landen waar de strafmaxima op dit moment hoger of juist lager zijn dan in Nederland?
Accepts the goal of harsher punishment but asks about the scale of smuggling, legal alternatives for refugees, the basis for the chosen increase, and how the 1999 WODC evaluation informed it.
They can agree with the aim of the bill to punish inhumane smuggling practices more harshly.
Zij kunnen zich vinden in het doel van het wetsvoorstel om mensonterende mensensmokkelpraktijken harder te bestraffen.
Shares the strict-approach premise but asks for the basis of the increase, comparison with trafficking penalties, and actual prosecution and sentencing levels.
At the same time, it is necessary to seek as objective a standard as possible for the height of the penalty.
Tegelijkertijd is het wel noodzakelijk om te zoeken naar een zo objectief mogelijke norm voor de hoogte van de strafmaat.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division recommends the bill raising maximum penalties for people smuggling proceed to parliament but asks for better justification of the deterrent effect, comparison with other EU member states, the urgency claimed, and the use of the urgent Referendum Act procedure. The minister's reply largely accepts these points by supplementing the explanatory memorandum, addressing EU penalty levels, and justifying urgency and the referendum-procedure use.
concerns: The Council asks for evidence that higher maximum penalties actually deter people smuggling, which the reply addresses with descriptive argument but no comparative empirical data.
The Council notes that a stronger prosecution policy does not require higher maxima and that no practical problems with current maxima are shown; the reply supplements the memorandum.

The Council asks the memorandum to address penalty levels in other EU member states and the expected effects of the increase on smuggling elsewhere; the reply adds a comparison and expects limited spillover.

The Council finds insufficient justification for urgency since smuggling is already punishable, and asks to revise the entry-into-force date if needed; the reply supplements the justification but no formal consultation of advisory bodies took place.

The Council asks for a sound justification for invoking the urgent procedure of article 12 of the Referendum Act, failing which it should be dropped; the reply supplements the justification and retains the procedure.

34363.s: The bill amends the Public Health Act and the Education Supervision Act so that municipalities performing youth health care can receive pupil personal data (name, birth date, school registration details) from the national education register BRON, on request. It also requires municipalities to destroy the data file within one month and extends the BRON data access provision.
34363.j: The memorandum justifies the new data access by the need for accurate, current pupil data for effective youth health care and states that a constitutional necessity and proportionality test under Article 10 of the Constitution was carried out.
q: Because it concerns providing personal data, a statutory basis is required under Article 10 of the Constitution.
Omdat het gaat om het verstrekken van persoonsgegevens is op grond van artikel 10 van de Grondwet een wettelijke basis nodig.
p: Artikel II A (artikel 24f, twaalfde lid, Wet op het onderwijstoezicht)
Municipal executives gain access to pupils' personal data from the national education register for youth health care purposes, limited to a specified list of data fields and a stated purpose.
Artikel I A (artikel 5, derde en vierde lid, Wet publieke gezondheid)
Municipalities must use the BRON data and must destroy the copied data file within one month, a retention limit that constrains the executive.

parties: Asks how JGZ access to absence data and other relevant records can be used in the child's interest, and stresses that parents and pupils must be carefully informed about data sharing.
The interests of the child and parents are paramount for these members in assessing this proposal.
Het belang van kind en ouders staat voor deze leden voorop bij de beoordeling van dit voorstel.
Questions the need for access to private data of all pupils, asks which data would become visible, and asks whether parents should be informed or give consent.
These members ask whether the government believes parents should be informed or should consent when BRON data are shared with JGZ.
Genoemde leden vragen of de regering van mening is dat ouders geïnformeerd worden of toestemming moeten geven wanneer gegevens uit het BRON met de JGZ gedeeld worden.
Asks how JGZ may use BRON data for its monitoring role when the law limits use to administrative invitation, and asks whether JGZ can access data of children outside their own municipality.

These members note in the article-by-article explanation, however, that the personal data from BRON may be used exclusively for the administrative process of inviting pupils to receive youth health care.

Deze leden lezen in de artikelsgewijze toelichting echter dat de persoonsgegevens uit het BRON uitsluitend gebruikt mogen worden voor het administratieve proces van het uitnodigen van leerlingen om jeugdgezondheidszorg te kunnen aanbieden.

34372.s: The bill amends the Criminal Code and Code of Criminal Procedure to allow investigators, with prior judicial authorisation, to covertly enter a suspect's computerised system remotely to identify it, record data, render data inaccessible or intercept communications for serious offences. It also orders providers to render certain data inaccessible, criminalises grooming and handling of data obtained through crime, and makes online trade fraud a punishable offence.
34372.j: The memorandum justifies the new covert entry power by the inadequacy of existing powers against encryption, cloud storage and networked devices, and by the seriousness of computer crime.
q: The entry may only be carried out for the purpose of performing certain investigative acts.
Het binnendringen kan uitsluitend worden verricht met het oog op het verrichten van bepaalde onderzoekshandelingen.
d: Artikel II, onderdeel L (artikel 126nba, achtste lid)
rules on use of the covert entry power where storage location is unknown
Artikel II, onderdeel L (artikel 126nba, zevende lid)
authorisation and expertise of investigating officers; automated logging of execution
storage, placement and removal of technical devices and their technical requirements
p: Allows prosecutors to order covert remote entry into suspects' computer systems, with only a prior written authorisation by the investigating judge as safeguard.
Lets the public prosecutor order service providers to render data inaccessible, subject to prior authorisation by the investigating judge and a complaint procedure.
Extends covert system entry to persons reasonably suspected of involvement in organised crime, with the same prior-authorisation safeguard.
Extends covert system entry to terrorism investigations on indications of a terrorist offence.
Provides a complaint route against orders to render data inaccessible and lets the court lift such orders.

parties: Argues the powers can protect privacy and trusts police to use them properly, but stresses internal oversight within the police and the hack unit must be in order.
Secondly, internal oversight within the police and the hack unit in particular will need to be in order.
In de tweede plaats zal met name het interne toezicht binnen de politie en de hack unit op orde moeten zijn.
Supports updating investigative powers but insists their use must be surrounded by safeguards and used restrainedly, questioning whether less intrusive powers are considered first.
However, the use of powers, especially where privacy or the safety of internet users is at stake, should only be surrounded by the necessary safeguards and used with restraint.

Echter, het gebruik van bevoegdheden dient, zeker als daarmee de privacy of de veiligheid van de internetgebruiker in het geding is, slechts met de nodige waarborgen omkleed en terughoudend ingezet te worden.
Not convinced of the necessity given the far-reaching infringement on fundamental rights and asks whether less intrusive alternatives exist.
They are first of all still not sufficiently convinced of the necessity of this bill, mainly because of the far-reaching infringement on fundamental rights.
Zij zijn allereerst nog steeds niet voldoende overtuigd van de noodzaak van dit wetsvoorstel, vooral vanwege de vergaande inbreuk op de grondrechten.

Supports swift entry into force and warns against further weakening of the powers, especially opposing removal of the decryption order, while asking about the rechter-commissaris review added to the bill.
They urge the government firmly not to heed various voices, including some parties and experts, calling to weaken the proposed powers further.

Zij vragen de regering met klem geen gehoor te geven aan diverse geluiden, zoals geuit door enkele partijen en deskundigen in het hierboven genoemde rondetafelgesprek, om de voorgestelde bevoegdheden nog verder af te zwakken.
Has serious objections to hacking via software vulnerabilities, questioning the contradiction of keeping security flaws open and the necessity of the broad powers.
Especially regarding covertly gaining access by using technical vulnerabilities, these members have serious objections.
Vooral bij het heimelijk toegang verschaffen door gebruik te maken van technische kwetsbaarheden, hebben deze leden grote bezwaren.
Asks about the scope of the term geautomatiseerd werk and whether the broad definition is adequately justified.
These members believe the necessity of the broad scope of this term requires further justification.
Deze leden menen dat de noodzaak van een brede reikwijdte van het genoemde begrip nadere onderbouwing vraagt.
Concerned about fundamental and practical problems of covert hacking and how it fits with rule-of-law principles, asking for case evidence of where existing powers fell short.
Warns that exploiting software vulnerabilities weakens online security for everyone and that the bill's breadth could allow disproportionate privacy intrusion, including on third parties.
This bill makes disproportionately large inroads on the privacy of Dutch citizens and seriously undermines online security.
Dit wetsvoorstel maakt buitenproportioneel veel inbreuk op de privacy van Nederlanders en tast de onlineveiligheid ernstig aan.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advises on the Computercriminaliteit III bill, which expands powers for covert remote entry into computers and includes a decryption order for suspects. The Afdeling finds the covert intrusion power insufficiently differentiated for proportionality under the EVRM, urges structural system oversight, and questions the effectiveness and nemo tenetur compatibility of the decryption order; the government reply largely accepts the remarks, revising the bill and dropping the decryption order.
concerns: The covert intrusion power is insufficiently differentiated by intensity of privacy intrusion, so proportionality under the EVRM is not established; the government adjusted the thresholds.
The decryption order for suspects conflicts with the nemo tenetur principle and EHRM case law; the government dropped the decryption order.
The necessity and effectiveness of the decryption order were not convincingly motivated; the government withdrew it in favour of covert intrusion.

Structural system oversight of investigative powers using ICT in cases not brought before a judge is recommended; the government did not adopt a structural oversight body, relying instead on existing safeguards.
The bill should specify the locus of the device and the rules for intrusion abroad and for data obtained; the government added conditions and explanation.
Placement of the power in the Titel IVA special investigative powers and the technical requirements provision were adjusted as advised.

34390.s: The bill amends the Dutch Civil Code by introducing a statutory presumption that physical damage within the affected area of gas extraction from the Groningen field was caused by that extraction, shifting the burden of proof to the operator. It also provides that the affected area is set by ministerial regulation, and that the presumption applies to damage that occurred before the law takes effect.
34390.j: The memorandum justifies the presumption by the large number and similarity of damage cases in Groningen and the need for flexibility in the affected area, which is therefore left to ministerial regulation while legal certainty is secured by a fixed reference date.
q: Therefore, for the sake of flexibility, it has been chosen to lay down the affected area by ministerial regulation.
Daarom wordt er, ten behoeve van de flexibiliteit, voor gekozen het effectgebied bij ministeriële regeling vast te leggen.
d: delineation of the affected area (effectgebied) of Groningen gas extraction
p: Creates a presumption of causation that favours damaged citizens against the operator and strengthens their legal position, subject to inspection and access conditions and a defined affected area.

parties: Asks how the presumption of damage causation relates to the Commissie Bodemdaling findings and how contour disputes will be avoided.
These members ask the government how it will prevent disagreement arising over the contours.
Deze leden vragen de regering hoe zij hiermee voorkomt dat er onenigheid ontstaat over de contouren?
Questions why the presumption applies only to Groningen and whether the burden of proof is too heavy for individuals across the Netherlands.
Is it correct that the aim should be to better balance the legal positions of the parties, particularly because the burden of proof for a private individual against a mining company is far too heavy?
Klopt dat het doel zou moeten zijn het meer in evenwicht brengen van de rechtsposities van partijen, met name omdat de bewijslast voor een particulier tegenover een mijnbouwbedrijf veel te zwaar is?
Argues the bill does not solve the problem for residents outside the contour map and for complex damage cases, and asks for a broader effect area.
People outside the contour map, who are currently not regarded as victims of gas-extraction damage, also fall outside the new proposal.
Mensen buiten de contourenkaart, die immers nu niet gezien worden als slechtoffer van schade door gaswinning, vallen ook met het nieuwe voorstel buiten de boot.
Welcomes the reversed burden of proof but asks for a central desk for damage outside Groningen and an evaluation after two years.

For the reasons above, these members ask the government to evaluate the reversal of the burden of proof in the Groningen effect area and the functioning of the central desk for possible mining damage two years after this amendment enters into force.

Om bovengenoemde redenen vragen deze leden de regering om de omkering van de bewijslast in het effectgebied in Groningen en het functioneren van het centraal loket voor mogelijke schade door mijnbouw nadat deze wetswijziging twee jaar in werking is, te evalueren.
Asks what the presumption means in practice for a specific damage case and whether it applies only to the Groningen field.
Is it correct that this introduction of the presumption applies only to the Groningen field?
Klopt het dat deze invoering van het bewijsvermoeden alleen van toepassing is op het Groningenveld?

Criticises the government for watering down the Vos/Ouwehand amendment, the Raad van State advice and the ministerial-regulation method of defining the effect area, and asks parliament to be involved.
The PvdD members consider it desirable that the House remain involved in determining the area.
De leden van de PvdD-fractie achten het wenselijk dat de Kamer bij het vaststellen van het gebied betrokken blijft.
Supports the presumption but asks why it is limited to Groningen when other mining areas have similar problems, and why immaterial damage is excluded.
They ask, however, why the introduction of the statutory presumption is limited to the province of Groningen.
Zij vragen echter waarom de introductie van het wettelijk bewijsvermoeden zich beperkt tot de provincie Groningen.
Asks how arbitration agreements, appeal rights and enforcement affect residents' legal protection, and whether the NAM can invoke lack of arbitral jurisdiction.
Can the government indicate whether a standard arbitration agreement will be drawn up?
Kan de regering aangeven of er een standaard arbitrageovereenkomst wordt opgesteld?
Asks how the veiligheid weigerings grounds are defined and whether limiting the presumption to Groningen creates unequal treatment.
These members ask whether limiting the presumption to Groningen and gas extraction will not lead to legal inequality with other residents of the Netherlands affected by mining activities.

Deze leden vragen of het beperken van het bewijsvermoeden tot Groningen en gaswinning niet zal leiden tot rechtsongelijkheid met andere inwoners van Nederland die te maken hebben met mijnbouwactiviteiten.
Raises a few questions without taking a clear position.
They have a few further questions.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised that the bill creating a statutory presumption of causation for mining damage in the Groningen gas field, which applies only to damage not yet known at entry into force, needed reasoned justification for its retroactive (eerbiedigende) effect and an explanation of costs for mine operators. The minister's reply states the bill was changed so the presumption also covers damage already known at entry into force, and the explanatory memorandum was supplemented on business burdens.
concerns: Retroactive effect of the presumption was not sufficiently justified given the principle of immediate effect; the bill was amended to cover damage already known at entry into force.
The explanatory memorandum did not address the burdens on mine operators from the bill; this was added.

34408.s: The bill replaces the Wet arbeidsvoorwaarden grensoverschrijdende arbeid with a new Wet arbeidsvoorwaarden gedetacheerde werknemers in de Europese Unie, implementing the posted-workers enforcement directive 2014/67/EU. It sets out working conditions for posted workers, a mandatory notification system for posting employers, cross-border administrative cooperation and mutual assistance, and administrative fines enforced by the Minister of Social Affairs and Employment through the Inspectie SZW.
34408.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations and data-sharing powers by the need for effective enforcement against social dumping and sham posting, the EU directive's requirements, and privacy safeguards tied to proportionality and necessity.
q: It is in the interest of bona fide service providers and their clients that potentially dishonest service providers are identified so they can be checked and, where necessary, acted against.

Het is in het belang van bonafide dienstverrichters en hun opdrachtgevers dat juist de potentieel malafide dienstverrichters in beeld komen zodat zij gecontroleerd kunnen worden en zo nodig worden aangepakt.
d: defining seafaring personnel and shipping companies
rules on data processing and retention for cross-border cooperation
elements for assessing genuine business activity and temporary work
form, language and timing of posting notification
exempting categories of workers and employers from notification
designating an independent administrative body for notifications
requirements for documents kept at the workplace
designating competent officials for mutual assistance
grounds for refusing foreign collection requests
further rules on minimum wage and working conditions for posted workers
p: Introduces a mandatory notification regime for posting employers and self-employed persons, with the state gaining detailed administrative information and the Minister given broad discretion over its design and exemptions.
Allows officials to process and share personal data on posted workers and employers with foreign authorities and other bodies, with details left to a general administrative order.
Lets inspectors assess whether an undertaking is genuine and whether a worker is temporarily posted, using elements set by administrative order.
Enables the Netherlands to enforce and collect foreign administrative fines via dwangbevel, with grounds for refusal set by administrative order.

Sets administrative fines up to fourth-category amounts with escalating surcharges for repeat violations, fine levels determined by ministerial policy rules, and allows the court to increase fines even to the detriment of the appellant.
Allows the Minister to share notification and cross-border data with employer and union bodies and private compliance organisations for enforcing collective agreements.

parties: Doubts whether the proposed changes will improve enforcement or only raise burdens for employers, and asks about the administrative cost of the notification duty.

The VVD members, however, have doubts about both the efficiency and the effectiveness of the proposed amendments and ask whether the burdens on entrepreneurs will not be increased without enforcement actually improving and fraudsters escaping.

De leden van de VVD-fractie hebben echter vraagtekens bij zowel de doelmatigheid als de doeltreffendheid van de voorgestelde wetswijzigingen en vragen of de lasten voor ondernemers niet worden vergroot zonder dat de handhaving effectief zal worden verbeterd en fraudeurs weg zullen komen.

Supports the bill but argues a fundamental revision of the posting directive is needed, and asks whether the government will take national measures if EU proposals are insufficient and about the risk of pressure on posted workers acting as contact persons.

However, they are of the view that a more effective approach to exploitation, displacement and unfair competition requires, alongside this bill, a fundamental revision of the posting directive as well.

Zij zijn echter wel van mening dat voor een effectievere aanpak van uitbuiting, verdringing en oneerlijke concurrentie naast dit wetsvoorstel ook een fundamentele herziening van de detacheringsrichtlijn noodzakelijk is.

Asks for the draft AMvB defining elements to prevent bogus self-employment to be sent to parliament and asks how parliament will be kept informed about progress on cao core provisions, and about enforcement staffing.
The SP members ask the government to send to the House the draft of the general administrative order (AMvB) that will contain 'elements' to prevent bogus self-employment.

De leden van de SP-fractie vragen de regering de uitwerking van de algemene maatregel van bestuur (AMvB) waarin «elementen» worden opgenomen om schijnzelfstandigheid te voorkomen in concept aan de Kamer te zenden.

Supports protecting posted workers but asks about the relationship between the notification duty and A1 certificates, the criteria for risk sectors, and the timeline for the digital notification system.
The CDA members ask the government to elaborate on this limited notification duty and on which measures are taken to limit administrative burdens and prevent unnecessary thresholds.

De leden van de CDA-fractie vragen de regering om nader in te gaan op deze beperkte meldingsplicht en welke maatregelen er genomen worden om de administratieve lasten te beperken en onnodige drempels te voorkomen.

Questions the necessity of a notification duty for self-employed foreigners who may be unaware of it, asks about the severity of sanctions and whether first offences in good faith could be warned rather than fined.
The D66 members ask how severe the sanction is if a self-employed person is unaware of the notification duty and does not register when taking up an assignment in the Netherlands.
De leden van de D66-fractie vragen hoe zwaar de sanctie is als een zelfstandige niet op de hoogte is van de meldingsplicht en zich niet meldt bij het aannemen van een opdracht in Nederland.
Asks whether the government finds it desirable to clarify at EU level that cao wages belong to the hard core, and asks whether sanctions will be weighed against the circumstances of each case.
The SGP members ask whether the government considers it desirable that it be clearly arranged at European level that paying cao wages belongs to the hard core of wage components.
De leden van de SGP-fractie vragen of de regering het wenselijk vindt dat in Europees verband helder wordt geregeld dat het betalen van cao-loon tot de harde kern behoort van looncomponenten.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advises proceeding with the Dutch bill implementing the EU enforcement directive on posted workers, but asks for justification of extending information duties to self-employed persons, reconsideration of the scope and fine levels, and clearer rules on data protection and delegation. The government's nader rapport accepts several points, such as converting a discretionary power into an obligation and clarifying minimum wage components, but rejects or only partly follows others, including the self-employed extension and the removal of the ministerial power to designate an autonomous body.
concerns: Extending the notification duty to all self-employed in risk sectors needs convincing justification of necessity and proportionality; the government added justification but kept the extension.
The bill must show that the duties applied to self-employed are necessary given the freedom to provide services; the government clarified reasons of general interest.
Fine levels for information-duty breaches, including for self-employed, are disproportionately high and should be lowered; government says it will align amounts through a policy rule.
Criteria for designating risk sectors should be set in the law itself rather than delegated; government declined and kept criteria in the amvb.
Delegating ministerial tasks to an autonomous administrative body needs motivation and statutory basis; government removed the provision as advised.
Clarify the relationship between the notification duty under the Wet arbeid vreemdelingen and the new duty; explanatory memorandum supplemented.

Requirement that documents be kept at the workplace should be checked against the directive's proportionality and electronic-handling criteria; government kept on-site requirement with limited changes.
Specify the privacy safeguards for data processing by regulation in the amvb, including reference to the IMI regulation.
Various redactional points on definitions, references and the transposition table; most incorporated, some not.

34426.s: The bill replaces the Comptabiliteitswet 2001 with a new Comptabiliteitswet 2016 that sets out rules for budgeting, financial management, reporting and audit of central government finances. It also covers management and ministerial supervision of public liquid funds and public financial resources outside central government, and the structure and powers of the Algemene Rekenkamer.
34426.j: The explanatory memorandum justifies delegations as necessary for practical detail and modernisation without new burdens, and states the bill grants no additional burdensome powers relative to the 2001 Act.
q: Since this revision of the Comptabiliteitswet does not grant burdensome tasks and powers compared to the Comptabiliteitswet 2001
Aangezien deze herziening van de Comptabiliteitswet geen verzwarende taken en bevoegdheden ten opzichte van de Comptabiliteitswet 2001 toekent
d: detailed rules on budgeting, financial administration and reporting
rules on organisation and tasks of finance ministry unit and Auditdienst Rijk
further rules on management of public liquid funds outside central government
rules on ministerial supervision of public financial resources outside central government
Minister of Finance may set amounts and exempt legal persons from mandatory treasury banking
Minister of Finance sets thresholds for exemption from pre-notification of private law transactions
p: Minister of Finance may designate which legal persons with statutory tasks must bank with the treasury and may exempt them.
Ministers gain supervisory powers over public financial resources managed outside central government, including subnational bodies.

parties: Asks why strengthening parliament's budget right is not an explicit aim, and why budget flexibility is absent from the bill.
Criticises the lack of control over premium-financed spending and the absence of explicit effectiveness aims and evaluation duties in the bill.
A growing share of state funds goes to the premium sectors, but there is no possibility of control over effective or efficient spending.
Er gaat een groeiend deel van de rijksmiddelen naar de premiesectoren, maar er is geen controle mogelijk op de doeltreffende dan wel efficiënte besteding.
Worries that the global character of the bill reduces parliament's ability to supervise subordinate regulation and asks for stronger budget amendment and budget-right safeguards.
The SP members ask whether keeping the law global does not reduce the budget right of the House.
De leden van de SP-fractie vragen of het globaal houden van de wet het budgetrecht van de Kamer niet verminderd.
Expresses disappointment that premium-financed spending is excluded and asks for better oversight of health spending and of premium estimates.
The CDA members express their disappointment that it has not been further substantiated why premium-financed budget expenditure could not fall under the Comptabiliteitswet.

De leden van de CDA-fractie spreken hun teleurstelling uit over het gegeven dat niet nader is onderbouwd waarom de premiegefinancierde uitgaven van de begroting niet onder de Comptabiliteitswet zouden kunnen vallen.
Welcomes modernisation but asks why the bill does not strengthen parliament's budget right, clarify ministers' financial responsibilities, or integrate the Wet houdbare overheidsfinanciën.
Notes the changes are less fundamental than expected and asks whether the bill improves parliament's information position and the execution of budget amendments.
Did the government also aim, in modernising the Comptabiliteitswet, to improve the information position of the House, the ChristenUnie members ask.
Heeft de regering bij het moderniseren van de Comptabiliteitswet ook het verbeteren van de informatiepositie van de Kamer tot doel gehad, zo vragen de leden van de ChristenUnie-fractie.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on the draft new Comptabiliteitswet 201X, which modernises the Dutch public accounting law but was judged not yet ready for submission, mainly due to drafting problems, vague delegations, and an expansion of audit powers over non-state bodies that it advised against. The Minister's nader rapport accepts most remarks, removes chapters and delegations, but keeps a narrower expansion of Algemene Rekenkamer powers over contract partners and state holdings.
concerns: The Afdeling advised dropping the expanded investigative powers of the Algemene Rekenkamer over contract partners and organisations outside the state, which the government only partly accepted by limiting them to purchases tied to public tasks.

The Afdeling warned that broad, vaguely defined inspection powers over organisations, natural persons and tax reductions undermine the balance with respect for the private sector; the government clarified the objects but retained extended powers.
The Afdeling objected to open-ended delegations to the Minister of Finance, such as the power to designate categories of obligations outside the saldibalans, and the government dropped that power.
The criteria for mandatory treasury banking and vague terms like derde partijen and bepaalde publiekrechtelijke voorschotten lacked clarity, and the government sharpened the provisions.
Remarks on structure, definitions, the order of chapters, and wetgevingstechnical errors were largely accepted and the bill was revised accordingly.

The Afdeling said the stated aim of a less maintenance-sensitive, slimmer law was not achieved, since more detailed provisions were added at statutory level; the government moved internal rules to lower regulation and HAFIR.

34435.s: The bill re-introduces, for a further four years until 1 January 2020, the statutory target of at least 30% women and 30% men on the boards and supervisory boards of Dutch companies, with a duty to consider balance in appointments and a reporting duty in the directors' report. It includes a sunset clause removing these provisions on 1 January 2020.
34435.j: The memorandum justifies the extension by pointing to the importance of diversity at the top of Dutch business and the announced intention to extend the target, with an evaluation planned in 2016 and 2019.
q: The bill provides that the target is reintroduced for the period until 1 January 2020.
Het wetsvoorstel regelt dat het streefcijfer opnieuw wordt ingevoerd voor de periode tot 1 januari 2020.

parties: Asks whether including the target in the law has contributed to better representation of women and whether the government's sanctioning passage is a warning to business.
These members ask whether the passage on sanctions in the explanatory memorandum should be seen as a warning to business.
Deze leden vragen of de passage over sanctionering in de memorie van toelichting moet worden gezien als een waarschuwing aan het bedrijfsleven.
Asks what criteria define non-compliance and why sanctions were not included in this bill despite insufficient progress.
These members ask the government which criteria, and to what extent, it considers decisive for speaking of non-compliance.
Deze leden vragen de regering welke criteria in welke mate in haar ogen maatgevend zijn om te spreken van niet-naleving.
Worries the bill is a step toward a definitive gender quota and questions whether threatened sanctions are the right route, given the compliance costs for firms.
The bill, however, appears to be a prelude to a definitive women's quota, a drastic measure the CDA members would prefer to keep well away from.
Het wetsvoorstel lijkt echter een opmaat tot een definitief vrouwenquotum, een paardenmiddel waar de leden van de CDA-fractie zich liever verre van houden.
Asks whether the limited growth in women on boards results from the statutory target or would have occurred anyway, and whether research was done.

The members ask whether the limited growth achieved is the result of the statutory provision the government now wants to extend, or whether it is gradual growth that would also have occurred without this law.

De aan het woord zijnde leden vragen of de beperkte gerealiseerde groei het resultaat is van de wettelijke bepaling die de regering nu wil verlengen of dat hier sprake is van een geleidelijke groei die ook zonder deze wet zou zijn gerealiseerd.
Notes that 57% of firms do not explain non-balance and that no sanctions apply, asks why a temporary target is chosen again and what enforcement the government will use if it fails.

Member Klein questions the current state of affairs and asks to what extent the government considers the current reporting obligation a dead letter, since no sanctions currently attach to failing to prepare such a report.
